item.title: Second pillar: the Union calls for a CH-IT comparison
item.description: The Unione Frontalieri Italiani calls for a comparison between Italy and Switzerland on the second pillar, a central issue for cross-border workers' pension provision.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Unione Frontalieri Italiani calls for talks - The topic is the second pillar - The talks involve Italy and Switzerland
## Key facts - Subject → Unione Frontalieri Italiani - Topic → second pillar - Request → talks with Italy and Switzerland
### The request and scope
The Unione Frontalieri Italiani calls for talks with Italy and Switzerland on the second pillar. This is the central fact of the news: for the worker who crosses the border, the discussion concerns Swiss occupational pension provision and how it is considered together with the other components of the employment relationship.
In Swiss pension terminology, the second pillar corresponds to the LPP. It is not the same item as the AVS and should not be confused with the LAMal, which concerns health insurance. For a frontier worker with a G permit, this distinction helps interpret deductions correctly and avoid adding together institutions that serve different purposes.
The LPP contribution rate ranges from 7 to 18% depending on the age bracket, starting at 25 years of age. This figure does not replace checking the individual position, but it explains why the second pillar has a tangible weight in the discussion requested by the Union. Verification must start with the LPP item, not with a generic deduction from the salary.
The AVS also has its own item: the employee share for AVS/AI/IPG is 5,3%. INPS, on the other hand, belongs to the Italian system. Comparing LPP, AVS and the INPS position without separating the different levels risks making the situation of the worker in Canton Ticino difficult to understand.
The topic is fully cross-border. The worker may have an employment relationship in Switzerland, residence in Italy and a G permit, but the news indicates a request for talks on the second pillar. It does not, by itself, announce a new rule for the payslip, a new rate or a deadline.
To follow the pension dossier without confusing pensions, taxes and health insurance, it is advisable to start from guida ad AVS e LPP. The talks between Italy and Switzerland can be understood correctly only by keeping occupational pension provision separate from the other aspects of cross-border work. ### Three levels not to be conflated
The request for a comparison becomes understandable when the cross-border worker separates pension provision from taxation. The items that appear in the employment relationship do not all have the same function and do not apply according to the same logic.
| Item | Practical reference | |---|---| | LPP | 7-18% by age bracket, upon reaching age 25 | | AVS/AI/IPG | 5,3% paid by the employee | | AD/AC | 1,1%, with a limit of CHF 148'200 | | Withholding tax | withheld only in Switzerland; tax credit in Italy in the CE section of the 730 tax return |
The table helps isolate the pension aspect. If the worker looks at monthly net pay, LPP should not be confused with AVS or AD/AC; if they look at tax matters, they should not turn the credit mechanism into a double withholding. For employment income, withholding tax is withheld only in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit indicated in the CE section of the 730 tax return.
### The tax dates to keep separate
The phrase new tax agreement 2026 should also be used with caution. The Nuovo Accordo Frontalieri was signed on December 23, 2020, has been in force since January 1, 2024, and Italy ratified it with Law 83 of June 13, 2023. These are dates relating to the tax framework, not to the LPP calculation.
The distinction between old and new cross-border workers affects how income is interpreted. Anyone who was already a cross-border worker before July 17, 2023 falls under the 7.500 euro exemption provided for by the 2024-2033 transitional regime. For new cross-border workers, the tax-free allowance is 10.000 euro. This comparison does not change the nature of the second pillar: it serves to avoid confusing the tax rule with occupational pension provision.
For a worker in Canton Ticino, therefore, the question to ask is not only how much is withheld, but which institution each item belongs to. LPP, AVS, withholding tax and double taxation require separate readings; LAMal remains a separate chapter. A guida alla dichiarazione dei redditi helps keep the tax path separate from the pension path.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ### Four operational steps
1. Set the reference date. Note whether you were already a cross-border worker before July 17, 2023. This step guides the distinction between old and new cross-border workers: in the former case, the 7.500 euro exemption under the 2024-2033 transitional regime applies; in the latter, the allowance is 10.000 euro.
2. Separate the social-security items. Read LPP and AVS/AI/IPG on separate lines. For LPP, take the age bracket into account, because the applicable rate ranges from 7 to 18% from the age of 25. Also keep AD/AC separate, set at 1,1% up to the CHF 148'200 limit. Do not include LAMal in the same block: it serves as health insurance.
3. Reconstruct the tax process. For employment income, withholding tax is deducted only in Switzerland. In the Italian filing, the tax credit in Section CE of the 730 serves to prevent double taxation. This is the point to check when comparing Swiss net pay and the Italian tax return, without adding the same tax twice.
4. Set out the agreement dates chronologically. The New Cross-Border Workers Agreement was signed on December 23, 2020, ratified in Italy by Law 83 of June 13, 2023, and has been in force since January 1, 2024. The chronology prevents 2026 from being mistaken for the entry-into-force date and helps correctly interpret the relationship between taxation and LPP.
This guide allows the cross-border worker to approach the comparison with organized data: status, date, social-security item and tax treatment. For the permesso G e B check, the administrative matter remains separate; guida ad AVS e LPP is available for pension matters.
To estimate the effect of the items on monthly net pay, use calcolatore dello stipendio netto.
*Source: [vconews.it](https://www.vconews.it/2026/10/05/leggi-notizia/argomenti/economia-e-lavoro-9/articolo/secondo-pilastro-lunione-frontalieri-italiani-chiede-un-confronto-con-italia-e-svizzera-1.html)*

item.title: Double currency seizure at the Brogeda border crossing
item.description: At the Brogeda border crossing, in two separate operations, customs officers and financial police officers from Ponte Chiasso intercepted over 240mila euro in recent days.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Two separate operations in recent days - Over 240mila euro intercepted - Customs officers and financial police officers from Ponte Chiasso - The location is the Brogeda border crossing ## Key facts - What → double currency seizure - When → in recent days - Where → Brogeda border crossing - Who → customs officers and financial police officers from Ponte Chiasso - Amount → over 240mila euro In recent days, at the Brogeda border crossing, customs officers and financial police officers from Ponte Chiasso intercepted over 240mila euro. The report refers to two separate operations and therefore presents a double currency seizure, not a single episode described as a unified event. The key point is the combination of location, personnel and amount. Brogeda is the border crossing indicated in the headline and the text; Ponte Chiasso identifies the customs officers and financial police officers involved in the two operations. The figure is expressed as over 240mila euro: this conveys a threshold, not an exact sum to be attributed to the entire episode or divided between the two operations. The headline and the text agree on the operation's dual nature and on the indicated location. The time reference is deliberately broad: the source speaks of recent days and does not place the two interventions on a calendar date. The phrase separate operations merely clarifies that the cases are separate; it does not make it possible to establish whether they occurred on the same day or at different times. ### The scope of the news report The text remains focused on these elements. It does not add names, vehicles, motives, operational methods or consequences following the seizure. Nor does it indicate any change for those crossing the border, or mention closures, queues or detours. For the cross-border commuter, the actual link is therefore the location of the news: Brogeda is a crossing point located in the territorial area of Canton Ticino, but the source does not describe effects on the daily commute. This distinction also matters in the choice of words. It can be said that the money was intercepted in two operations and that the headline presents them as currency seizures. It is not possible, however, to reconstruct the reason for the intervention, establish who was carrying the amount, or infer which procedure was followed. Anyone seeking operational information about crossing can consult tempi di attesa ai valichi, keeping that data separate from the news report: the source here does not report travel times or disruptions. ## How to interpret the data regarding over 240,000 euros For a cross-border commuter, the news is of limited practical interest but is verifiable: it concerns a border crossing, not a regulation on cross-border work. The text allows us to establish the location and the economic scale indicated, but not to transform the seizure into an update on wages, permits, or taxes. ### Certain data and interpretations to avoid | Element | Correct interpretation | | Two distinct operations | The seizure concerns two separate operations | | Over 240,000 euros | The amount is above the indicated threshold, not an exact figure | | Customs and financial police of Ponte Chiasso | These are the operators indicated by the source | | Brogeda border crossing | This is the location reported in the news | The table helps to avoid taking an extra step. The source does not link the episode to the G permit, AVS, LPP, or LAMal. It does not mention INPS, withholding tax, tax rebates, or double taxation. These topics cannot be used to explain why the currency was stopped: the text does not provide a motive. The same caution is needed regarding traffic. Knowing that there were two operations at the border crossing does not allow one to state that traffic was slowed down, that additional checks were implemented, or that cross-border commuters had to change their route. None of these elements appear in the source. To check a potential traffic situation, one must use separate information, such as the traffic history and queues at border crossings, without attributing it to this news. There is also no before-and-after comparison. The source does not indicate a new rule, a deadline, a general ban, or a change for those working in Ticino. Therefore, the practical analysis stops at a precise point: the cross-border commuter recognizes the location and the operation but does not derive personal obligations, effects on their paycheck, or consequences for their permit from the brief text. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Procedure for correctly using the news The operational response is not a new customs procedure, because the source does not describe one. For those who work in Ticino and pass through Brogeda, it is best to read the brief report as a fact sheet with a few verifiable details. The following procedure serves to avoid turning a headline into information that the text does not contain. ### Five control steps 1. Start with the location. The reference is the Brogeda border crossing. Do not replace it with other border crossings or a different municipality: the source does not extend the case to other locations. 2. Preserve the sequence. The operations are two and distinct. This wording should be maintained when reporting the news, without merging them into a single inspection and without assigning the same amount to each. 3. Respect the figure. The source says over 240mila euro. Writing exactly 240mila or dividing the sum between the two operations would add information that is not present. 4. Identify the personnel. Customs officers and financial police officers from Ponte Chiasso are identified. No individual names or other offices appear, so none should be added. 5. Separate the report from the consequences. The text does not indicate documents to submit, deadlines to meet, penalties, traffic blockages or effects on cross-border workers. It is not possible to derive a personal checklist from the announcement alone. This method is also useful for updating an internal communication or deciding which information to look for next. First verify whether independent data exist on the crossing; then keep the news within its limits. The reference to Brogeda does not automatically become a traffic advisory, just as a currency seizure does not become an update on AVS, LPP or withholding tax. If your objective is instead a separate check of the tax calculation for the salary, use calcolatore fiscale and not this report as a basis for adding details to the Brogeda case. *Source: [laregione.ch](https://www.laregione.ch/estero/confine/1954732/doppio-sequestro-di-valuta-al-valico-di-brogeda)*

item.title: Varese Observatory: the Galileo show arrives
item.description: On Saturday, October 17, the G.V. Schiaparelli Observatory will host Corrado D'Elia's play, followed by observation of the Moon and Saturn.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Show at the Varese Observatory on Saturday, October 17 - The Corrado D'Elia theater company on stage - After the play, observation of the Moon and Saturn - Saturn also visible through the Galilean telescope replica ## Key facts - Event → Saturday, October 17 - Location → G.V. Schiaparelli Astronomical Observatory - Show → «Galileo, Beyond the Stars» - Company → Corrado D'Elia - Area → Varese Campo dei Fiori - After the play → astronomical observation session - Celestial objects → Moon, Saturn and other celestial objects - Historical instrument → replica of Galileo's telescope On Saturday, October 17, the «G.V. Schiaparelli» Astronomical Observatory in Varese, at Campo dei Fiori, will host «Galileo, Beyond the Stars», the show by the Corrado D'Elia theater company. The company, active in Milan's major theaters, is coming to Varese for the first time with a work dedicated to the Italian scientist. The event presents a theatrical narrative described as intimate and revolutionary, structured as a journey through science, art and freedom. The performance is hosted in a special venue, the G.V. Schiaparelli Astronomical Observatory in Varese Campo dei Fiori, and offers an unusual perspective on the figure of the great Italian astronomer. ### The evening at the Observatory The title of the show indicates a journey that goes beyond a simple biography. The narrative in fact explores Galileo from a particular perspective and places the theatrical story in a space dedicated to observing the sky. The event will not end with the play. The program also includes an astronomical observation session, linking the theatrical story to the opportunity to look at the sky from the Varese venue. The session will take place at the end of the show and will be conducted using the Observatory's instruments. For Corrado D'Elia, therefore, the event marks the first time this show about the Italian scientist comes to Varese. For the audience, the offering brings together theater and observation on the same evening, without separating the story dedicated to Galileo from the astronomical experience scheduled after the performance. ## Galileo portrayed on stage ### Research, doubt and freedom The core of the play is the question of who Galileo Galilei really was, beyond the myth of the genius, the heretic, and the man who dared to challenge heaven and earth. The story also questions the price of research and what lies behind the image of the scientist capable of changing our view of the universe. The presentation of the show evokes the words «And yet it moves», whispered with determination and despair and, over the centuries, becoming a symbol of freedom of thought. This reference gives shape to a portrait that looks not only at Galileo’s public persona, but also at the questions and anxieties of the man. Corrado D'Elia guides the audience in discovering a more human Galileo than ever. In the story, the scientist is first and foremost a man: a son, a father, a lover, a solitary and restless thinker. He is a person capable of marveling at the stars and endlessly questioning the meaning of the universe. The narrative thus attempts to enter the soul of a complex and extraordinary character. His story is read through an inner struggle, in which the torment of the intellect is measured against dogma, and the need to survive comes into conflict with the instinct to seek the truth. The picture presented is that of an era marked by the clash between science and faith, freedom and power, knowledge and fear. The company presents «Galileo, Beyond the Stars» as a journey into these contradictions, but also as the portrait of a man who forever changed the vision of the cosmos and existence, leaving a legacy still capable today of prompting those who contemplate it to question themselves. ## Observation after the play ### The Moon, Saturn and the replica of the telescope At the end of the performance, the program will continue with an astronomical observation session through the Observatory's telescopes. Participants will be able to admire the Moon, the planet Saturn and several other celestial objects. The initiative places alongside modern instruments a replica of the telescope made by Galileo Galilei in 1609. Saturn will also be visible through this instrument, allowing contemporary observation to be compared with the perspective of those who scrutinized the sky at the beginning of the 17th century. The experience on offer concerns not only the object being observed, but also the characteristics of the instrument. The replica has limited capabilities and a restricted field of view, features that recreate the conditions of an observer in the early 1600s. With a telescope of this type, however, Galileo succeeded in making discoveries destined to change forever the way the universe was viewed. The concluding session therefore takes the audience from the theatrical narrative to the practice of observation, with the opportunity to examine a replica of the Galilean instrument and the Observatory's telescopes. The Moon, Saturn and the other celestial objects will be the tangible continuation of the play dedicated to the Italian scientist. Booking is mandatory to attend the event. The evening is therefore divided into two stages: first the performance by Corrado D'Elia's company, followed by the astronomical observation at the headquarters of the G.V. Schiaparelli Astronomical Observatory in Varese Campo dei Fiori. *Source: [varesenoi.it](https://www.varesenoi.it/2026/10/05/leggi-notizia/argomenti/eventi-20/articolo/allosservatorio-astronomico-di-varese-arriva-lo-spettacolo-galileo-oltre-le-stelle.html)*

item.title: Mental health: DSS brings prevention into companies
item.description: DSS and Forum GSA Ticino promote mental health at work. Data: 32,3% of young people in Ticino feel drained, 61% of apprentices are suffering.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - DSS and Forum GSA Ticino strengthen prevention - 32,3% of active people aged 25-34 in Ticino report feeling emotionally drained - 61% of Swiss apprentices experience mental health problems - Free workshops on October 16, upon registration ## Key facts - Promoters → DSS and Forum GSA Ticino - Recipients → Ticino companies, apprentices and trainers - Proposals → mental health in companies and Apprentice - Event → October 16 - Participation → free, upon registration In Bellinzona, the Department of Health and Social Affairs (DSS) is strengthening its commitment to promoting mental health through a collaboration with Forum GSA Ticino, which is active in workplace health management. The initiative brings awareness-raising, information and training activities to Ticino companies, with the aim of fostering work environments focused on well-being and offering tools to those who work there. If a cross-border worker works for one of the companies concerned, the relevant context is therefore the workplace. The source does not distinguish between residents and cross-border workers and does not present a measure linked to place of residence: it describes an offering aimed at Ticino companies, with training sessions open to all interested organizations. For those living across the border, the page on vivere in Svizzera remains a separate in-depth resource; this article concerns prevention in the workplace. ### Work as a place of well-being > «Mental health is a fundamental component of people’s well-being and health», reads the DSS note. The Department recalls that, in addition to individual behaviors and choices, life contexts also contribute to well-being. The workplace is one of the places where working people spend a significant part of their lives: it should enable them to feel well, develop skills, find meaning in what they do, feel supported and cultivate positive relationships. The data cited in the communication paint a complex picture. Promozione Salute Svizzera’s regular survey on work-related stress indicates that about one third of the working population in Switzerland is emotionally exhausted and has a critical level in the Job Stress Index, that is, an unfavorable ratio between workloads and available resources. Among working people aged 25-34, 32,3% in Ticino report feeling emotionally drained, compared with 24% of the Swiss average. The WorkMed survey, conducted in 2024, adds the apprenticeship dimension: 61% of apprentices in Switzerland experience mental health problems in a broad sense, and between 25% and 30% would need more active support. In Ticino, almost 1 apprentice in 3 reports anxiety disorders, while 86,9% would never have discussed them with the school or training company. The source interprets this latter figure as a sign of the difficulty of accessing available support. ## What it means for the worker ### An offer delivered through the company The news brings together two levels: the data describe people’s distress, while the proposed response is organized within companies. No individual assistance procedure is announced; instead, awareness-raising, information and training sessions are planned. If a cross-border worker is employed by an interested company, access therefore depends on the company initiative indicated by the source. The scope remains limited. The text provided does not mention permit G, AVS, LPP, LAMal or withholding tax. There is therefore no textual basis for attributing effects on taxation, social security, insurance or commuting to the collaboration. For permesso G/B, a different in-depth analysis is needed; here, the only verifiable link is employment in companies in Canton Ticino. | Proposal | Target audience | Stated content | |---|---|---| | Mental health in companies | Managers, human resources managers, interested employees | Training on the topic | | Apprentice | Apprenticeship trainers | Knowledge and practical tools; Health Promotion Switzerland program adapted to Salutepsi.ch | | October 16 event | Interested companies | Breakfast meeting and afternoon workshop, free of charge upon registration | This distinction avoids confusing the target audiences. The first proposal is aimed at those with responsibility for or a direct interest in company management; Apprentice instead supports people who accompany young people during their apprenticeship. The program is not presented as a tax or social security solution, but as a way to strengthen knowledge and skills in managing health in the workplace. The topic also has an economic dimension: work-related stress entails estimated costs of about 6,5 billion francs per year for the Swiss economy. The source links the potential economic benefits of reducing stress to this figure, without quantifying results for individual companies or workers. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## How to proceed ### Four practical steps The press release makes it possible to identify a course of action without adding details that were not provided. For those who work across the border, the prerequisite remains a Ticino-based company: the source does not describe an individual registration linked to the place of residence. 1. Define the company's interest. The offer is aimed at all interested Ticino companies. A cross-border worker can therefore start with their own organization, without turning the news into a personal procedure that the source does not describe. 2. Match the proposal to the role. Executives, human resources managers and interested employees turn to training on mental health in companies. Apprenticeship trainers, on the other hand, find the Apprentice program, designed for those who support young people during their apprenticeship. 3. Choose the event. A breakfast meeting and an afternoon workshop are planned for October 16. Both are part of the day dedicated to mental health proposed by Promozione Salute Svizzera and Forum GSA Ticino. 4. Complete the registration. The two events are free and open to all interested companies, but require advance registration. This is the operational requirement explicitly stated by the source. The sequence separates access from content: first the company signs up, then the recipient follows the proposal that matches their role. In the case of apprenticeships, the material is designed for people who support apprentices and aims to provide concrete knowledge and tools. The collaboration ultimately aims to foster conditions that contribute to young people's mental health and the organization's well-being. To complete your guidance on working in Ticino, use the calcolatore stipendio. *Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/ticino/attualita/1954714/stress-e-salute-mentale-il-dss-porta-la-prevenzione-nelle-aziende-ticinesi)*

item.title: Undeclared cash: seizures at Brogeda
item.description: Two checks at the Como-Brogeda motorway border crossing led to the seizure of 128.500 and 113.450 euro, amounts exceeding the threshold of 10.000 euro.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Over 240 thousand euros intercepted in two checks - The first seizure amounted to 128.500 euros - The second seizure involved 113.450 euros - The indicated currency threshold is 10.000 euros ## Key facts - Location → Como-Brogeda motorway border crossing - Who → Gruppo Ponte Chiasso of the Guardia di Finanza - First discovery → 138.255,53 euros - Second discovery → 123.431,45 euros - First seizure → 128.500 euros - Second seizure → 113.450 euros - Competent authority → Ministry of Economy and Finance More than 240 thousand euros in cash were intercepted in two separate operations at the Como-Brogeda motorway border crossing. The operation was carried out by personnel from the Gruppo Ponte Chiasso of the Guardia di Finanza. The checks involved two different groups of travelers and ended with the seizure of the amounts exceeding the 10.000-euro threshold provided for by current currency regulations. ### The first operation In the first check, a couple of travelers declared that they were carrying a modest amount of cash intended for the purchase of a property in Spain. However, the declaration did not indicate possession of amounts equal to or greater than 10.000 euros. The authorities reported detecting inconsistencies in the statements provided and, for this reason, the officers conducted a more thorough inspection of the vehicle. The inspection led to the discovery of 138.255,53 euros in cash, in various denominations and currencies. The money was kept in a pouch concealed beneath some luggage. The officers therefore seized 128.500 euros, representing 100% of the amount exceeding the permitted limit. ### The subsequent check A few days later, personnel from the Customs and Monopolies Agency and members of the Guardia di Finanza checked two other travelers. They too declared that they were carrying an amount below the threshold established by law. The inspection was extended to the vehicle and, while the luggage was being checked, 123.431,45 euros in cash were found inside a shopping bag. In this second incident, the seizure of 100% of the excess, amounting to 113.450 euros, was ordered. The sums seized in the two operations were held as security for the administrative penalties. Their amount is to be determined by the Ministry of Economy and Finance, which is also responsible for imposing them. For those crossing the border by car, the practical reference remains the border crossing indicated in the report; tempi di attesa ai valichi are available to arrange the crossing. For a cross-border worker crossing Brogeda, it is useful to define the scope. The source does not address the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, INPS or withholding tax: it describes the transport of cash, the currency threshold and vehicle checks. This distinction avoids conflating the incident with cross-border employment taxation or social security. ### The declaration does not end the inspection The two incidents show the same operational step, but in different ways. In both cases, the travelers declared a modest sum or an amount below the prescribed threshold. Subsequent checks, however, led to the discovery of higher amounts. The useful point for anyone passing through the border crossing is therefore the correspondence between what is declared and the cash actually carried in the vehicle. The first case mentions the purchase of a property in Spain; in the second, the report focuses on the inspection of two other travelers. The first cash was in a small pouch hidden under the luggage, while the second was in a shopping bag. The difference concerns the place where the cash was found, not the outcome: in both interventions, 100% of the amount exceeding the threshold was seized. The first inspection led to the seizure of 128.500 euro out of 138.255,53 euro found; the second to 113.450 euro out of 123.431,45 euro. The first discovery included various denominations and currencies. For a separate exchange-rate check, the site provides comparatore di cambio, which does not replace the declaration at the border crossing. ### Seizure and penalty are two different stages The sums are not described as an already determined penalty. They were retained as security for the payment of administrative penalties, which will be determined by the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the authority responsible for imposing them. For the cross-border worker, this distinguishes the immediate outcome of the inspection from the subsequent stage indicated in the source. The certain fact is the retention of the seized sums. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. To read the case as a practical sequence, the cross-border worker passing through Como-Brogeda can follow only the steps documented in the two interventions. ### Five steps described by the source 1. Verify the amount being carried. The threshold cited is 10.000 euro. The source links it to the current currency regulations and refers to amounts equal to or greater than that limit. 2. Declare the cash consistently with what is present in the vehicle. In the first episode, a modest sum was declared; in the second, an amount below the threshold. In both cases, the inspection subsequently revealed larger sums. 3. Bear in mind that the inspection may extend to the vehicle and luggage. In the first intervention, a small bag beneath some luggage was checked; in the second, a shopping bag. These are the locations indicated in the source. 4. Distinguish the amount found from the amount seized. In the first case, the figures reported are 138.255,53 euro found and 128.500 euro seized; in the second, 123.431,45 euro found and 113.450 euro seized. In both episodes, the seizure amounted to 100% of the excess. 5. Consider the subsequent phase. The seized sums are held as security for payment of the administrative penalties. The source attributes the determination and imposition of the penalties to the Ministry of Economy and Finance. This sequence keeps the inspection, the seizure of the excess and the penalty phase separate. It is the operational criterion that emerges from the two checks and should not be confused with a guide to taxation for cross-border employment. To organize the crossing, consult mappa dei valichi. item.title: Truck breakdown in the San Nicolao tunnel
item.description: A truck breakdown in the San Nicolao tunnel is causing disruptions on the A2: the left lane is passable southbound and delays of up to 20 minutes northbound.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Truck breakdown in the San Nicolao tunnel - Disruptions on the A2 southbound - From Grancia, only the left lane is passable - Delays of up to 20 minutes northbound
## Key facts - Event: truck breakdown - Location: San Nicolao tunnel, Melide - Southbound: only the left lane from Grancia - Northbound: TCS reports congestion between Mendrisio and the tunnel - Delays and traffic conditions: up to 20 minutes; traffic lights in operation
Melide is the point from which this Monday morning's traffic update begins. A truck breakdown in the San Nicolao tunnel is causing disruptions to traffic on the A2 southbound. The report therefore concerns the stretch of motorway where the tunnel is located and asks motorists to allow for delays.
The effects on traffic are already being felt near Grancia. From that point, according to the report, only the left lane is passable. The reference to Grancia identifies the point at which the effects on southbound traffic are already evident.
The traffic situation also includes the opposite direction. Northbound, TCS reports congested traffic between Mendrisio and the same tunnel, with delays of up to 20 minutes. The notice also states that the traffic lights are in operation. item.description: Sunday, October 4, around twenty motorcycles and three cars took over via Appennini for speed races and wheelies. Carabinieri officers from Besozzo intervened.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Around twenty motorcycles and three cars on Via Appennini - Wheelie, speed and handbrake braking contests - Residents called 112 - Immediate intervention by the carabinieri from Besozzo Station ## Key facts - Location → Via Appennini, Cocquio Trevisago - Date → Sunday, October 4 - Event → unauthorized gathering of motorcycles and cars - Participants → around twenty motorcycles and three cars - Motorcycle trials → timed wheelie contests - Car trials → speed and braking - Report → residents and condominium residents in the area - Intervention → carabinieri from Besozzo Station ### The trials on Via Appennini Around twenty motorcycles and three cars gathered on Sunday, October 4, on Via Appennini, in Cocquio Trevisago, for an unauthorized gathering. The gathering included various trials, with specific activities for motorcyclists and car drivers. The motorcycles took part in timed wheelie contests. The cars, on the other hand, competed in speed and braking trials. For these maneuvers, the drivers used the handbrake to make quick U-turns and immediately resume the race. The reconstruction therefore distinguishes between two modes: on the one hand, timed wheelies, and on the other, driving trials based on speed, braking and quick U-turns. The source describes the gathering as unauthorized. The presence of the vehicles on Via Appennini was connected to the contests described. There were three cars involved, while there were around twenty motorcycles, according to the reconstruction of the incident. Some residents and condominium residents in the area raised the alarm. The citizens called 112 and reported the situation to the carabinieri from Besozzo Station. The report came while the trials were underway and led to the immediate intervention of law enforcement. The first documented step was therefore the residents' call, followed by the arrival of the carabinieri in the Via Appennini area. The text places the gathering, the motorcycle and car maneuvers, the residents' alarm and the intervention of Besozzo Station in this sequence. The initial phase of the reconstruction focuses on the incident and the immediate response to the report. ## The local context For residents and condominium owners, what happened on via Appennini adds to incidents already observed. The source reports that the previous Sunday some residents had witnessed similar scenes. When the gathering took place again, the call to 112 therefore came from people who had already seen the same kind of behavior in the area. The issue highlighted by residents concerns not only motorcycle and car maneuvers. In the same area, more abandoned waste and cars left there were found, described in the source as car wrecks. The deterioration is associated with a road that has to coexist with these elements and with the repeated reports. ### Reports about the waste The waste that was found was probably dumped during the weekend of September 26 and 27. Here too, the source uses cautious wording: it indicates a probable period, without attributing the dumping to a specific person or group. A similar situation had been reported in mid-September. The sequence of time references is the one reported in the account: a similar report in mid-September, then the weekend of September 26 and 27 indicated as the possible time when the waste was dumped, followed by the new report linked to the gathering on Sunday, October 4. It is the residents of the area who, through their calls and their mobilization, link the condition of the road to the incidents observed. ### A private road for public use Via Appennini is described as a private road for public use. The phrase sums up the local issue described by the source: the space is private, but used by the public, and has to coexist with waste and car wrecks. The area's 54 «condominium owners» mobilized, asking the institutions for solutions and action. The source does not indicate what measures were decided, but documents the collective request and the repeated reports about the area's deterioration. ## The aftermath of the intervention The Carabinieri's check had different outcomes among the participants. One young man managed to escape. The first hypothesis reported is that he may have avoided the check because he had no documents, no insurance, or a modified motorcycle. These possibilities are indicated as initial hypotheses and not as definitive findings. For the others present, however, the check ended with them being stopped and identified through their documents. The reconstruction therefore distinguishes the position of the young man who managed to escape from that of the other participants, who were stopped at the scene. The outcome described concerns the document check for the people who were stopped and one young man's escape from the check. ### The request of the 54 condominium residents Alongside the checks on the participants, the report records the mobilization of the area's 54 “condominium residents.” The residents are asking the institutions for solutions and action regarding the situation reported on Via Appennini. The request concerns a private road for public use, where the source reports the presence of car wrecks, abandoned waste, and new gatherings. The mobilization of the condominium residents gives the aftermath a collective dimension. It is not merely a matter of the check carried out after the call to 112: the report also refers to a request addressed to the institutions by the 54 condominium residents. The documented aftermath therefore consists of an intervention by the Carabinieri with different outcomes for the participants and a request for solutions for the area. The source places both elements in connection with the situation described on Via Appennini. *Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/raduno-di-moto-e-auto-non-autorizzato-in-via-appennini-a-cocquio-trevisago-carabinieri-in-azione/2698036/)*

item.title: Cash seizure in Como-Brogeda: over 240 thousand euro
item.description: More than 240.000 euro in cash seized at the Como-Brogeda border crossing by ADM and the Guardia di Finanza in two separate operations.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - More than 240.000 euro intercepted at the Como-Brogeda border crossing - Two inspections by ADM and Guardia di Finanza - 128.500 and 113.450 euro seized - Cash hidden in a pouch and a bag ## Key facts - Where → Como-Brogeda motorway border crossing - Who → ADM and the Gruppo Ponte Chiasso of the Guardia di Finanza - Threshold → 10.000 euro - First discovery → 138.255,53 euro - First seizure → 128.500 euro - Second discovery → 123.431,45 euro - Second seizure → 113.450 euro - Penalties → determined by MEF More than 240.000 euro in cash was intercepted in recent days at the Como-Brogeda motorway border crossing, on the border with Canton Ticino. The money was uncovered in two separate operations carried out by personnel from the Agenzia delle Dogane e dei Monopoli’s Distaccamento Locale di Ponte Chiasso and by officers from the Gruppo Ponte Chiasso of the Guardia di Finanza. The activity was part of daily checks on cross-border currency movements along the border with Switzerland. To help navigate the crossing, the website also offers the tempi di attesa ai valichi. ### The first operation The first inspection involved a couple of travelers. During the check, the two stated that they were carrying a modest sum intended to purchase a property in Spain. They did not declare possession of amounts equal to or exceeding 10.000 euro, the threshold referred to in currency regulations and linked in the press release to Legislative Decree no. 195/2008. The statements revealed inconsistencies. The officers therefore carried out a more thorough inspection of the vehicle and, beneath some luggage, found a concealed pouch containing 138.255,53 euro in cash, in various denominations and currencies. Pursuant to Article 6 of the cited legislation, 128.500 euro was seized, indicated as 100% of the amount exceeding the permitted limit. ### The second operation A few days later, in the same operational setting, two other travelers stated that they had cash with them in an amount below the threshold established by law. An inspection of the luggage led to the discovery, inside a shopping bag, of 123.431,45 euro. In this case too, 100% of the excess was seized: 113.450 euro. The seized sums were held as security for payment of the administrative penalties, pending the conclusion of the proceedings. The Ministero dell'Economia e delle Finanze is identified as the authority competent to determine and impose them. Guardia di Finanza and Agenzia delle Dogane e dei Monopoli presented the operation as an example of institutional synergy against the illicit cross-border movement of cash at border crossings. ## The point for those crossing the border For a cross-border commuter crossing the border, the practical aspect of the news is not a change to the payslip, but the handling of cash during the crossing described by the source. The press release links both cases to declarations below the threshold of 10.000 euro and to subsequent checks of the vehicles. In the first operation, inconsistencies in the declarations are also mentioned; in the second, a thorough check of the luggage brought the shopping bag to light. The news therefore concerns physical money transported through the border crossing. ### What the press release clarifies The sequence has a concrete effect on how the episode is interpreted. The initial declaration and the physical discovery do not coincide in the two cases: the declared amounts are described as below the limit, while the inspections lead to the discovery of larger sums. The press release then indicates a precise consequence, the seizure of 100% of the excess, not an administrative penalty that has already been defined. The sums remain held as security, and the amount of the penalties must be determined by MEF. This is the procedural stage described; the text does not indicate a final decision. The scope is equally important. The communication provides no information on G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, withholding tax, tax rebates, INPS, the new 2026 tax agreement or double taxation. These are issues different from the movement of cash across the border. Anyone looking for the rules governing Permesso G/B will not find in this episode a change to permits or social security. For the cross-border commuter traveling from Canton Ticino to Italy, the takeaway is therefore limited: the check concerns the currency being carried, the stated threshold and any possible excess. For geographic orientation alone, mappa dei valichi is available. The source does not say that every traveler is subject to seizure, nor does it describe forms, documents or channels for obtaining authorizations. On these aspects too, it is not correct to supplement the news with rules that are not present. ## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## The procedure that can be reconstructed The source makes it possible to derive an operational sequence limited to the established facts. To avoid confusing the case with a broader tax guide, the cross-border worker can read it in five steps. ### Five steps 1. Identify the checkpoint: the Como-Brogeda motorway border crossing, where ADM and Guardia di Finanza took action. 2. Distinguish the declaration made by the travelers: in both interventions, a sum below the threshold of 10.000 euros was declared; in the first case, the intended use for purchasing a property in Spain was also indicated. 3. Consider the subsequent verification: in the first episode, the inconsistencies led to an inspection of the vehicle; in the second, a thorough check of the luggage led to the discovery of the money. 4. Separate the cash found from the amount seized: the source indicates, in both cases, the seizure of 100% of the sum exceeding the permitted limit. 5. Consider the provisional outcome: the sums remain held as security, while the proceedings must be finalized and the penalties will be determined by MEF. This is the only procedure that can be reconstructed from the press release. No forms to fill out, specific documents, offices to contact, deadlines for concluding the proceedings, or timeframes for returning the sums are indicated. Including these elements would mean adding information unrelated to the source. For those who cross the border for work, the practical reading therefore remains focused on consistency between the declaration and the cash being carried, without turning the two episodes into a general rule about the outcome of every check. The report documents two separate interventions and the related measures adopted, not a complete procedure for every traveler. To follow the next crossing, consult tempi di attesa ai valichi. *Source: [varesenoi.it](https://www.varesenoi.it/2026/10/05/leggi-notizia/argomenti/cronaca-20/articolo/nascondevano-in-auto-denaro-contante-in-un-borsello-e-in-una-busta-della-spesa-sequestrati-240-mila.html)*

Boccadamo drove forward decisively down the right flank and whipped in a cross for Chessa, who beat Leoni from close range with a precise header. It was the first incident in a match that was lively and hard-fought from the start. The black-and-green side continued to press. Three minutes after taking the lead, Schirò found the net after making the most of an assist from Chessa himself, but the referee disallowed the goal for offside against Castellanzese's centre-back. Sant'Angelo reacted first with a sliding effort from Nechita off a Garatti free kick, then levelled after fifteen minutes. Maltoni rose in the area and beat Bongini with a header. The visitors protested the play for an alleged foul on Matella. Castellanzese did not lose its shape. It continued to build from the back, moving the ball along the ground, and after the half-hour mark it threatened again. item.title: Varese, Magrini: 'The Province is already investing in culture'
item.description: President Magrini responds to the Region: a fund of 100 thousand euros has been allocated for the candidacy for Italian Capital of Culture and projects in the area.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Magrini defends the cultural investments of the Province of Varese - Fund of 100 thousand euros for new initiatives in the area - Over 30 million euros at the center of discussions with the Region - Varese relaunches its candidacy for Italian Capital of Culture President of the Province → Marco Magrini Call for applications → Province and Fondazione Comunitaria del Varesotto Cultural funding → over 30 million euros Fund → 100 thousand euros Province's share → 50 thousand euros Objective → put Varese forward for Italian Capital of Culture Partners mentioned → Chamber of Commerce and new Varese Welcome foundation Experimental service → Santa Caterina del Sasso ### The response to the Region Marco Magrini opened today's press conference of the Province of Varese, dedicated to the call for applications promoted by the Province together with the Fondazione Comunitaria del Varesotto, with a response to regional Councillor for Culture Francesca Caruso. The councillor, in an interview, had called for an ever-greater commitment from the cultural system of the local areas, describing it as a lever for development. Magrini said he acknowledged and shared the message, while maintaining, however, that the Province was already working in that direction and was aligned with the councillor's approach. In his remarks, the president recalled the commitments made together with the Region and, in particular, the funding project for culture worth over 30 million euros. The Province, he explained, had been involved in the project but was still awaiting decisions regarding the initiative. Magrini clarified that he had set a condition regarding the management of the resources and their local impact: > «The funds will have to be managed with clear rules, ensuring that the benefits accrue to the area of the province of Varese, not to the institution». The criterion indicated by the president therefore concerns both the rules and the recipient of the benefits. The declared objective is to ensure that any funding produces effects in the area of the province of Varese, rather than being attributed to the institution as such. Magrini then linked the possible positive outcome of the regional action to a specific destination. If the councillor manages to secure the funding, a significant part of the initiative will concern the Sacro Monte. The resources, the president added, could, however, also serve other areas. The response to Councillor Caruso thus formed part of the presentation of the work that the Province claims to have already begun. On the one hand, there is agreement with the request for a growing commitment to culture; on the other, a reference to the investments and projects that Magrini mentioned during the press conference. ### The interventions and places mentioned Later in the conference, Magrini listed the investments already put in place by the Province, offering a sequence of figures and places. The first reference is Santa Caterina del Sasso: the site received 600 thousand euros and then another 500 thousand euros, earmarked for infrastructure works. The president distinguished these resources from those linked to the Via Francisca, for which 900 thousand euros concern tenders for the route. Villa Recalcati, on the other hand, received one and a half million for safety measures. The three references were presented as part of the interventions through which the Province chose to invest in the area's heritage and places. Alongside the infrastructure works, Magrini mentioned the Mosaico project, carried out with the support of the Foundation. The initiative brought folk music to landmark places in the province, including the cloister of Voltorre and Villa Recalcati. In his account, the project thus sits alongside the resources earmarked for material works and broadens the picture of the cultural activities supported. This list gave rise to the challenge addressed to the Region. Magrini argued that the Province is making significant resources available and asked that the Region do the same. The request was not accompanied by new regional figures: the president referred to the funding proposal still awaiting decisions and indicated the provincial investments already completed or launched. Magrini ultimately asserted a choice made several years ago: to invest in local areas and concrete projects, working in harmony with mayors and foundations. According to his explanation, this approach produced benefits for the entire province. It is along these lines that the president said he had changed gear, linking the resources allocated to cultural sites with closer collaboration between local institutions and foundations. ## The fund and Varese's bid The fund presented during the press conference is the instrument intended for new initiatives to promote the area. The Province will make 50 thousand euros available and the Fondazione Comunitaria del Varesotto will double the amount, bringing the fund to 100 thousand euros. The activities indicated by Magrini include books, films and documentaries dedicated to the history of important places. Initiatives related to music, poetry and exhibitions are also planned. The fund's purpose is therefore described in broad terms, with different proposals all aimed at promoting the area. The final goal indicated by the president is to bring these actions together in order to put Varese forward as Italian Capital of Culture. Magrini presented the bid as a challenge that also requires the support of the regional councillor for Culture Francesca Caruso. The reference to the Region thus returns in the next phase of the project, after the discussion on investments and cultural funding of over 30 million euros. ### A network between culture and mobility The strategy outlined also includes working as a system. The partners mentioned by Magrini include the Chamber of Commerce and the new Varese Welcome foundation, with which integrated communication work is planned. The project therefore concerns not only individual sites, but also how to present them through collaboration among different entities. Among the projects already launched is the connection with local public transport. For Santa Caterina del Sasso, an experimental service has been activated which, given the interest it has generated, could be structured as early as next year. The idea put forward by the Province is to connect the area's main cultural sites through an integrated system. The project includes Santa Caterina del Sasso, the cloister of Voltorre and the area's museums. The connection should include a single ticket and integrated organization. The fund, communication with partners and local public transport are therefore the steps described by Magrini to give shape to the bid. ## TL;DR - Bellucci loses the Jingshan final in the deciding tiebreak. - Two match points squandered at 6-5 in the third set. - Harris wins the tiebreak 7-4 after 2 hours and 20 minutes. - The player from Varese should rise to number 86 in the ATP rankings from Monday. ## Key facts - Tournament → Jingshan Open, China - Level → Challenger - Final → Mattia Bellucci-Lloyd Harris - Surface → Hard court - Deciding tiebreak → 7-4 for Harris - ATP points → 50 regained by Bellucci Mattia Bellucci lost the final of the Jingshan Open in China, a Challenger tournament played on hard court. The player from Varese was defeated by South African Lloyd Harris after 2 hours and 20 minutes, at the end of a match decided only in the third-set tiebreak. The turning point came when the score was 6-5 to Bellucci. The Castellanza player, who served first in the deciding set, earned two consecutive match points on Harris’s serve. The experienced South African saved both and took the final to a tiebreak, which he closed out 7-4. The difference was therefore three points, in a set without a break. ### The match set by set The start had put Bellucci on course for the fifth Challenger title of his career. The left-hander won the first set 6-1, with tennis described as aggressive and allowing the opponent no chances. Harris, however, responded in the second set, winning 6-3 and restoring balance to the final. The Cape Town native brought his experience onto the court: in his career he has also beaten Nadal and was ranked number 31 in the world. item.description: The Order of Architects of Varese recounts the 2021–2025 restoration and the history of Torre Velasca through architecture, design, and redevelopment.

## TL;DR - Torre Velasca at the center of a meeting at Villa Recalcati - Conference hall of the Province of Varese packed with attendees - Restoration took place between 2021 and 2025 - Maniglia Velasca remained in the catalog until 2005 ## Key facts - Location → Villa Recalcati, Province of Varese - Promoter → Order of Architects of Varese - Project → Studio BBPR and engineer Arturo Danusso - Purchase → 150 million euros - Restoration → 2021-2025 - Handles → Olivari, catalog until 2005 The conference hall of the Province of Varese, at Villa Recalcati, hosted a meeting dedicated to Torre Velasca, the famous monumental building in Milan. The evening was promoted by the Order of Architects of Varese as part of the Olivari Openings series and attracted a substantial audience. The account followed three threads: the building's origins, the renovation project, and the history of the handle that became a symbol of the tower. The event opened with official greetings from Giorgio Caporaso, president of the design commission, and Michela Nurra, president of the Young People and Innovative Tools commission. Then Stefano Suriano, an architectural historian, took the audience inside the project by Studio BBPR and engineer Arturo Danusso. His interpretation highlighted a dual modernity: in the construction solutions and in the building's social significance. ### A housing model beyond the engineering challenge Torre Velasca was not presented solely as a technically complex work. According to Suriano's account, the tower brought together three different structures—commercial, office, and residential—and also proposed compact residential solutions. These included 40-square-metre one-bedroom apartments, a choice described as revolutionary compared with the standards and habits of living in the city center during the postwar period. The transition from the project to the present came with architect Giacomo Albo's contribution. Albo illustrated the phases of the renovation carried out between 2021 and 2025, documented with thousands of photographs requested by the latest purchaser. The redevelopment adapted the tower to contemporary times while respecting the original structure. The evening concluded with engineer Antonio Olivari, of the eponymous company, and with the story of the handles designed in the 1950s by Gio Ponti and Lodovico Barbiano di Belgiojoso, a member of Studio BBPR. Since then, that design has been known as «Maniglia Velasca». ## From the housing model to conservation The most significant point in the account is not a single date, but the way the speakers connected use, construction, and conservation. Torre Velasca was considered both as a technical building and as a housing model. The presence, in the same tower, of commercial spaces, offices, and homes describes a complex structure; the 40-square-meter one-bedroom apartments add a compact residential option to this complexity. According to the account of the evening, it is this juxtaposition that makes the project innovative on the social level as well. ### Philology as a working criterion As for the restoration, the keyword is «philology». Before the works, a meticulous inventory was made of everything inside the tower. The subsequent phase did not erase that survey: it led to the restoration of most of the original elements, from the wood paneling to the historic details of the staircases. The criterion described by Giacomo Albo therefore brings together two needs: adapting the building to contemporary times and remaining faithful to the original design. The economic dimension makes the construction site even more imposing. The redevelopment costs doubled the property's original purchase price of 150 million euros. This figure is inseparable from the documentation: the thousands of photographs requested by the last buyer recount the lengthy construction phase and accompany the transformation without replacing the existing structure. item.description: Openjobmetis wins 78-85 at Scafati, securing its first official victory of the season and its second ever on the Campania court.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Openjobmetis wins 78-85 in Scafati - Hale finishes with 25 points and 7 assists - This is the first official victory of the season - Wednesday BCL debut in Murcia ## Key facts - Result → 78-85 - Record in Scafati → second win ever - Season → first official victory - MVP → Hunter Hale, 25 points and 7 assists - First quarter → 17-24 - Halftime → 38-40 - Scafati free throws → 27 - Next commitment → Wednesday night in Murcia, BCL debut 78-85 at PalaMangano, Openjobmetis secured its first official victory of the season in Scafati and the second ever on the Campanian floor. The result gives Ioannis Kastritis his main objective, but leaves open questions regarding gameplay, choices, and defense. The final reaction was a sigh of relief rather than a shout of joy. The absence of two guaranteed starters and the incomplete condition of two others forced an emergency lineup. Duke joined Hale in the backcourt, Nikolic and Kamagate worked under the basket, and Alviti played in the middle. Scafati, missing Brandon Johnson, responded with Mascolo and McGruder off the bench, and Lever and Onyema under the boards. There were few people at PalaMangano, but the group of Varese fans was good, especially among the Arditi banners. ### The game quarter by quarter Hale immediately delivered the first push, also taking advantage of many turnovers by Longobardi. Midway through the period, the score was 4-8; Openjobmetis, despite missing shots, could have extended its lead further. Renfro and Kamagate made their contributions, and the first quarter ended at 17-24. The second period began with the best moment of the first half. Flying baskets by Renfro and Nikolic and an acrobatic drive by Villa brought Varese up by 13. Then Mascolo sparked the comeback. Kastritis called a timeout after a 15-2 run, with only a single red-and-white basket—by Nikolic—in six minutes. Hale limited the damage, and at halftime the lead was 38-40. In the third quarter, Hale and Duke scored a 5-0 run, but Moore responded with a three-pointer after a pump fake on Roby. Alviti scored from deep on his very first touch, while Renfro converted the balls received in the paint. When Scafati closed within two, Librizzi struck with two consecutive three-pointers, and Hale capped the break with a drive, making it 62-70. In the final period, Varese scored little, but controlled the boards better. Duke stepped up on both ends; Kamagate, despite not jumping much, was useful as a pivot in several plays. An electrical issue interrupted the final moments. The play at the 24-second buzzer and the ensuing free throw stretched the lead to 11. The factor that weighs most heavily is not just the score, but the way the game remained open. Varese conceded second-chance shots and trips to the free-throw line; Scafati had 27 free throws, missing many of them. The defense was thus faced with a constant choice: protect the paint or accept switches onto smaller players. ### The issue with defensive switches The system of systematic switching created favorable mismatches for Campania's perimeter players. Renfro and Kamagate were forced to chase smaller players away from the basket, leaving less protection inside the paint. Scafati found rebounds and second chances. In the fourth quarter, however, the red-and-whites paid more attention to rebounding and prevented the hosts from getting back within reach. On offense, the emergency at point guard remained evident. Openjobmetis made up for it with the flair of Hale, Duke and Librizzi, but individual plays did not conceal the difficulties in creating offense. Hale finished with 25 points and 7 assists, while Renfro was very effective; Alviti was barely involved from beyond the arc and Isaiah Roby delivered another poor performance. The second half showed the importance of Duke and Librizzi, not an already established collective solution. On Wednesday evening in Murcia, for their BCL debut, the bar will be higher. The Spaniards will not offer the same concessions found in Campania on three-point shooting, free throws and the management of turnovers. Kastritis described the team as a work in progress and emphasized the value of the away win. The technical consequence is clear: the result in Scafati must be backed up with more orderly playmaking, a less exposed defense and better management of the big men. The finale erased the risk of a cruel upset, but not the questions. The gap between summer Varese and October Varese, highlighted by the source, lies in these details: do not give away possessions, do not empty the paint and do not rely on a spectacular play for every solution. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. To follow the next step without stopping at the final result, it is advisable to turn the game into a step-by-step assessment. The source provides precise indications of what to observe, without the need to add numbers or outside scenarios. ### The checklist for Murcia First: look at the playmaking. Against Scafati, Kastritis had to play Duke alongside Hale, while Librizzi also made an impact in the second half. The point to watch is whether the offense will be able to involve more players or will still have to rely on individual ingenuity. Counting baskets is not enough: the construction of the offense will show how much the emergency is being felt. Second: check how far the big men are from the basket. Renfro and Kamagate were called on to chase the perimeter players after defensive switches. The check is simple: when they switch, can Varese protect the paint and control the rebound? Scafati's fourth quarter offered a positive sign on the second point, but the problem had been evident in the preceding minutes. Third: follow the possessions involving Roby and Alviti. Roby was coming off yet another poor performance, while Alviti was barely involved on the perimeter and hit a three-pointer virtually with the first ball he touched in the third quarter. The game in Murcia will show whether these episodes will remain isolated or whether the roles of the two players in building the offense will change. Fourth: put shooting, free throws and turnovers together. Scafati had 27 free throws and missed a lot; the source warns that Murcia may not offer the same concessions. It is therefore these three categories, together with rebounds, that must form the basis for assessing the change of gear. Fifth: assess the finish without being misled by the relief. In Scafati, the play on the 24-second buzzer and the subsequent free throw brought the lead to +11, after a power outage and a stretch in which the doubts were still alive. The answer to look for is a game that reduces the need to rely on the last play. Shortly afterward, StraWoman changed the color of the scene. Varese was crossed by a festive pink wave along the 5-kilometer route, with more than 3.000 women at the start. Among the people mentioned as being present were also Deputy Mayor Ivana Perusin and Budget Councillor Cristina Buzzetti. The morning is therefore described through two starts and two sporting images: the champions and cyclists of the Gran Fondo, followed by StraWoman's pink race. The common thread is the city center, which the source presents as the space given over to sporting passion. The cycling program, the parade of past champions and the presence of the institutions mentioned in the news coverage came together on Via Sacco. Shortly afterward, the StraWoman route brought its pink wave into the city's streets. The continuation of the morning is entrusted to the photo gallery. These are 94 shots by Alessandro Umberto Galbiati, collected to tell what the succession of numbers alone cannot convey: Varese's center transformed into a space dedicated to sport. The source presents the photographs as a more effective account than words. The images bring together the race, the pedals and the legs of a Sunday experienced in the heart of the city, without separating the Gran Fondo Tre Valli Varesine from StraWoman in the overall picture of the morning. The gallery thus brings together the two events. On one side is the cycling start on Via Sacco; on the other, shortly afterward, the festive pink wave along the 5-kilometer route. The photo feature preserves the visual impression of a Varese that, according to the source, stopped to make room for sporting passion. With its 94 photographs, Alessandro Umberto Galbiati's photo feature brings Sunday's story to a close, placing the city and the images at its center. This is the documented continuation: a gallery dedicated to a sporting morning, entrusted to the shots that tell of the presence of the cyclists, the women of StraWoman and the protagonists mentioned at the start. *Source: [varesenoi.it](https://www.varesenoi.it/2026/10/04/leggi-notizia/argomenti/fotogallery-12/articolo/foto-di-rosa-e-ciclismo-novantaquattro-scatti-di-una-varese-che-si-consegna-alla-passione-sportiv.html)*

item.title: Sport and legality at De Filippi with the Nazionale Ristoratori
item.description: A day of education, football and haute cuisine at the De Filippi hotel management institute in Varese with the chefs of the Nazionale Italiana Ristoratori.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR
- De Filippi welcomed NIR's chef-footballers - The event took place on Monday, September 28, in Varese - The discussion focused on the educational value of rules - The NIR-De Filippi match ended 2-3
## Key facts
- Participants → NIR and students of the De Filippi Institute - Location → via Brambilla 15, Varese - Coordination → Laura Broggi, principal of De Filippi - Match → 14.30, final score 2-3 - Conclusion → gourmet aperitif at 19
### A day between school and the restaurant industry
On Monday, September 28, the De Filippi hotel management institute in Varese hosted a day that brought together sport, education and the restaurant industry. The students met NIR's chef-footballers, the Nazionale Italiana Ristoratori, in a program held at the institute's premises at via Brambilla 15.
The initiative brought the hotel management school and the chefs' association together through several stages. The centerpiece of the event was the meeting on the theme «Sport and Legality – The educational value of rules», a discussion involving several voices coordinated by principal Laura Broggi. De Filippi students and NIR representatives gathered around that theme, focusing on the topics set out for the day.
The program did not stop at the discussion. In the afternoon, at 14.30, NIR's representative team faced a selection from the De Filippi Institute in a football match that later ended 2-3. In the evening, at 19, that same day concluded with a gourmet aperitif prepared by NIR's chefs with the support of the De Filippi fourth-year class.
The event's structure thus brought together the discussion of values, the on-field challenge and the work in the kitchen. These are three distinct stages, but part of the same initiative hosted by the institute in Varese: the discussion dedicated to legality, the sporting event and the final culinary moment. For the students, the program brought restaurant professionals to the school and offered them a multifaceted encounter with the world of NIR, without separating sport and education from the theme of hospitality. ## The discussion on the culture of legality
### Rules, hospitality and responsibility
The title “Sport and Legality – The educational value of rules” guided a discussion that was not limited to the competitive dimension. At the center was the importance of respecting the rules, identified as an educational value and linked to the culture of legality. The topic was addressed before the students of the De Filippi Hotel Management Institute, where future hospitality professionals are trained.
The discussion also touched on the value of hospitality and welcoming customers. These elements were presented together with training in food service, because the day connected the work of chefs with the students’ course of study. The source links these themes to the responsibility everyone has toward Italian cuisine, described as a heritage to be protected and enhanced.
Laura Broggi, principal of De Filippi, coordinated the discussion. Mauro Elli, president of the NIR, Michelin-starred chef and owner of the Il Cantuccio di Albavilla restaurant, took part in the debate. His colleagues from the association also participated. The discussion with the students made it possible to contextualize the themes of sport and food service within the broader topic of the culture of legality.
The point highlighted by the day therefore concerns the relationship between rules, hospitality and responsibility. Respect for the rules was addressed together with how a customer is welcomed and the shared responsibility toward Italian cuisine. For the students, the debate connected hotel management training with a reflection on the value of hospitality and the protection of a gastronomic heritage. The culture of legality was the framework within which the source places both sport and food service, with the involvement of the principal, the president of the NIR and the other chefs from the association. ## From the match to the gourmet aperitif
### The result on the field
At 14.30, the program entered its sporting phase. The NIR representative team faced a selection from the De Filippi Institute in a football match that ended with a score of 2-3. The score concluded the scheduled contest between the Nazionale Italiana Ristoratori team and the selection from the Varese hotel management institute.
The match gave concrete form to the participation of the chef-footballers in the day. On one side was the NIR representative team; on the other, the students chosen to represent De Filippi. The final result, 2-3, is the only sporting data reported for the match and completes the initiative’s transition from discussion of the rules to the challenge on the field.
### The closing in the kitchen
At 19, the day concluded with a gourmet aperitif. It was prepared by the NIR chefs, with the support of the fourth-year class at De Filippi. The class’s contribution also involved the students in the event’s gastronomic phase, alongside the professionals of the Nazionale Italiana Ristoratori.
Among others, Stefano Minervino took part in the aperitif; he is the chef-owner of the starred restaurant Condividere in Arona and a teacher at De Filippi. His role was indicated through both activities: on the one hand, ownership of the starred restaurant in Arona, and on the other, teaching at the institute involved in the day.
The sequence of events describes the initiative’s concrete continuation: at 14.30, football between NIR and De Filippi; at 19, the gastronomic conclusion with the fourth-year class and the chefs. The program thus paired the match with a haute cuisine moment, maintaining within the same event the presence of the Nazionale Italiana Ristoratori, the students and the hospitality professionals trained by De Filippi.
