item.title: Varese: Record-breaking Gran Fondo with 5.000 registrants
item.description: Tenth edition concluded on October 4: 2.000 foreign participants and victories for Ferraro Morey and Rumasaite.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 5.000 registered participants from over 25 nations - Approximately 2.000 athletes from abroad - Tenth edition concluded on Sunday, October 4 - Ferraro Morey and Rumasaite win the Granfondo ## Key facts - Event: Gran Fondo Tre Valli Varesine - Edition: tenth - Registered participants: 5.000 - Foreign athletes: approximately 2.000 - International participation: over 25 nations - Organizer: Società Ciclistica Alfredo Binda - Granfondo route: approximately 130 kilometers - Trophy: Fondazione Varese Welcome Five thousand registered participants from over 25 nations brought the tenth edition of the Gran Fondo Tre Valli Varesine to a new participation record. On Sunday, October 4, the Fondazione Varese Welcome Trophy closed out a weekend of great international cycling, with thousands of athletes competing across Varese and its province. Total registrations reached 5.000. The event thus brought together participants from Italy and abroad around a program combining sport, passion, and discovery of the area. The source puts the number of foreign athletes present at approximately 2.000 for the tenth edition. The weekend featured the Gravel Experience, the Individual Time Trial, the Gran Fondo and the Medio Fondo. The various events animated Varese and the Varesotto before Sunday’s conclusion, when the road races took place. The event’s route thus accommodated different formats while keeping amateur cycling at its center. The event was organized by Società Ciclistica Alfredo Binda, which celebrated its tenth edition with an event of even greater sporting prestige. Tre Valli Varesine was in fact the venue for the UEC Gran Fondo European Championships. The event was also part of the UCI Gran Fondo World Series calendar and the Gran Fondo Series Gobik circuit. The presence of the UEC European Championships extended across the entire weekend and gave the events held in Varese province international prominence. The tenth edition concluded after days featuring thousands of cyclists and participation that extended beyond Italy’s borders. On Sunday, the results of the Medio Fondo and Gran Fondo were decided. In the flagship event, victory went to Alessio Ferraro Morey; among the women, Lithuanian Rasa Rumasaite prevailed. Their wins brought to a close an event that the source describes as record-breaking in terms of registrations and international reach. The participation figure, together with the presence of the European Championships and international circuits, characterized the tenth edition of Tre Valli Varesine. Varese and its province provided the backdrop, with the weekend’s activities and the various competitions included in the program taking place across them. ## Results over the two distances Sunday's competition was divided between the Medio Fondo, with a course of approximately 100 kilometers, and the Gran Fondo, the premier event covering approximately 130 kilometers. The two races produced close finishes and standings also shaped by competition between different categories. ### The Mediofondo Among the men in the Mediofondo, Francesco Pirro won, also finishing first in category 19/34. His time was 2 hours, 35 minutes and 16 seconds. Matteo Foppiano finished behind him, just a few tenths back, while Emanuele Labate finished third, less than a second behind the winner. Foppiano and Labate also belong to category 19/34. The women's race was won by Michela Gorini, who crossed the finish line in 2 hours, 53 minutes and 45 seconds. Gorini belongs to category 50/54, but recorded the best overall result among the women. Jutta Stienen, also in 50/54, came second with a time of exactly 3 hours. Overall third place went to Anna Cadorin, of category 19/34, who stopped the clock at 3 hours and 5 seconds. ### The Granfondo The Gran Fondo took place over approximately 130 kilometers, among the climbs, descents and landscapes of the province of Varese. The course revisited some iconic locations from the 2018 Gran Fondo World Championships in Varese: Valganna, Valceresio, Lake Maggiore, Valcuvia and the return toward Varese. In the men's overall standings, Alessio Ferraro Morey, of category 19/34, won with a time of 3 hours, 10 minutes and 56 seconds. Giovanni Loiscio finished second and edged out Lucio Pierantozzi in the sprint. Both are in 19/34, and there were just 12 hundredths between them. The women's finish was even closer. Lithuanian Rasa Rumasaite won in 3 hours, 44 minutes and 2 seconds, also taking the 19/34 category. Martina Cavallo finished second and was the top finisher in 35/39. Frenchwoman Marion Bessone was third, also in 35/39. The first three women finished within just one second. The Gran Fondo result was accompanied by reported female participation of more than 400 registered athletes. The standings therefore combined Rumasaite's success, the competition between the 19/34 and 35/39 categories, and a minimal gap between the top positions. On the men's side, Ferraro Morey's victory came after a finish decided by equally close times for second and third place. ## An international race in the Varese area The international dimension of the tenth edition is evident from where the entrants came from. France, Belgium, Germany and the Netherlands were among the countries most strongly represented, but the list of participants also included athletes who arrived from the United States, Canada, Japan and Brazil. The event attracted approximately 2,000 foreign athletes out of 5,000 total entrants and received registrations from more than 25 countries. These figures also turned the Tre Valli Varesine into an opportunity to promote tourism in Varese and its province. The source pointed to the connection with the area alongside the sporting dimension: cyclists took part in the races and crossed the Varese area during a weekend built around the event's various formats. ### The role of Fondazione Varese Welcome This year, the collaboration with Fondazione Varese Welcome, which gives its name to the Trophy, is aimed precisely at strengthening the event's tourism dimension. The stated objective is to highlight the economic and tourism benefits for the area. The trophy's name thus links the cycling competition to the promotion of Varese and its province, without separating the sporting result from the discovery of the places touched by the races. The weekend began with Saturday morning's Gravel Experience, which attracted 400 entrants. It continued with the Individual Time Trial, in which 500 cyclists took part, and was completed with Sunday's road races. Taken together, these events brought thousands of people onto the roads of the Varese area. ### An event built with a local network The source attributes the result to Società Ciclistica Alfredo Binda, together with the institutions, partners and volunteers. The organizational work supported both the events on the programme and the European event hosted by the Tre Valli Varesine. The presence of the UEC European Championships made the transition from Saturday's competitions to Sunday's road races even more special. The balance sheet for the tenth edition therefore includes the participation record, the arrival of athletes from numerous countries and the intention to strengthen, through Fondazione Varese Welcome, the event's economic and tourism value for Varese and its province. *Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/gran-fondo-tre-valli-varesine-varese-capitale-del-ciclismo-amatoriale-la-decima-edizione-e-da-record/2697883/)*

item.title: Uyba make an even debut against Novara: Igor win in the tie-break
item.description: Laica Busto Arsizio lose 3-2 in the tie-break against Igor Novara at the Biella Forum in front of 1679 spectators; Grozer finishes with 26 points and Uyba earn a point.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Novara wins 3-2 in the tie-break - UYBA earns one point - At the Biella Forum: 1679 spectators - Grozer finishes with 26 points ## Key facts - Matchday → first matchday of women's Serie A1 - Venue → Biella Forum - Result → Laica Cioccolato UYBA-Igor Gorgonzola Novara 2-3 - Score → 25-22, 15-25, 19-25, 25-22, 12-15 - Spectators → 1679 - Grozer → 26 points - UYBA attack → 42% - Igor attack → 40%; Igor reception → 56% ### The derby at the Biella Forum The Ticino derby on the first matchday of the women's Serie A1 championship favored Igor Novara, but did not punish Laica Busto Arsizio. The Farfalle conceded only in the tie-break, handing two points to the Piedmont side and keeping one after a match that ended 2-3. The match was played at the Biella Forum, a venue chosen by the red-and-white club to make up for the closure of viale Gabardi. About 1.700 fans came for a fixture that is always keenly contested, while the scoresheet lists 1679 spectators. The different-than-usual venue did not change the tone of the match, which remained open until the final set. Laica, without Parra, started with the right rhythm. In the first set, Busto Arsizio led at the crucial moments and closed it 25-22. The set gave the home side the first lead of the evening, but Igor reacted immediately in the following set, won 15-25 by Tolok and her teammates. Starting with the third set, the contest became even again. Novara managed to pull away from Busto Arsizio late in the set, taking it 19-25. Laica responded in the fourth, in a head-to-head battle in which a single mistake could have shifted the momentum. The substitutions, with Marchesini and Torcolacci on court, and the courage of the red-and-white side brought the score to 25-22. The result thus sent the two teams to a fifth set. In the tie-break, Uyba held its own against its rivals for a long time, before a couple of wayward balls and an ace by Tolok altered the score. The concluding 12-15 gave Novara the victory, leaving Busto Arsizio with a point and regret over a match that slipped away only at the end. The split of the points reflects the course of a debut played point by point. Igor secured the win, but Laica made life difficult for the Piedmont side until the final action of the fifth set. ### The protagonists and the match data The individual performance of Laica centered primarily on Leana Grozer. The opposite hitter finished with 26 points, adding 4 blocks and 2 aces, and carried the Butterflies in a match in which Busto Arsizio also received contributions from her teammates. The Japanese player Wada, with 14 points, and Matilde Munarini and Battista, both on 10, also reached double figures. On the other side of the net, Tolok led Novara with 24 points. Her tally was complemented by Grobelna's 14 points and Squarcini's 14. The individual numbers explain the importance of the attackers in the decisive moments, without erasing the work of the red-and-white defense, described by the source as always highly reactive at the collective level. The statistical score sheet also compares the fundamentals of the two teams. UYBA recorded 4 aces, 14 service errors, 9 blocks, 42% in attack, 42% in reception and 31 total errors. Igor finished with 6 aces, 15 service errors, 14 blocks, 40% in attack, 56% in reception and 22 errors. The reported percentages therefore distinguish UYBA's 42% in attack from Igor's 40% in attack; the 56% instead concerns the reception of the Novara team. In Laica's case, the score sheet also indicates 42% in reception. These are figures that accompany the result without changing the reading of a match decided by the narrowest margin. Matilde Munarini linked the team's ups and downs to having had the full squad together for only four days, also emphasizing the determination shown on court: > «We are very satisfied with this match – Matilde Munarini explains – we have had many ups and downs, but I think that is normal given that we have had the full squad together for only four days. I particularly liked the desire to win that we showed on court; now we only need to refine our chemistry». The statement adds to the account of the score the issue of chemistry that still needs refining. For Enrico Barbolini's team, the source nevertheless speaks of encouraging signs after a debut that ended in a defeat, but with a point earned and a performance that remained competitive for five sets. ### The second matchday and the complete scoresheet The next reference given by the source for Uyba is the second matchday, which will see the team face Conegliano, described as unsinkable in the text. There are no other details about the fixture, while the report of the debut makes it possible to reconstruct the lineups used and the official data from the match. For Busto Arsizio, the scoresheet lists Battista with 10 points, Pelloni marked with the letter L, Malual did not play, Monaco, Marchesini with 6, Parlangeli did not play, Spaziano, Munarini with 10, Torcolacci with 4, Grozer with 26, Martínez Vela did not play, Seki with 3, Otomo with 1 and Wada with 14. The team was coached by Enrico Barbolini. The Igor Novara lineup included Cambi with 3 points, Herbots with 12, Squarcini with 14, De Nardi did not play, Weske did not play, Grobelna with 14, Alsmeier, Moro marked with the letter L, Bartolini did not play, Bonifacio with 11, Carraro, Tolok with 24, Perinelli and Awoleye did not play. The coach was Massimo Barbolini. The report also lists Piana and Serafin as referees. The sets lasted 29, 22, 25, 31 and 16 minutes, for a total of 2h 18′. These are the concluding elements of the sheet for a match that ended in the fifth set, with the 12-15 giving Novara the win. The second matchday against Conegliano therefore represents the next step cited for the Busto Arsizio team. The debut leaves Uyba with the work on team chemistry referred to by Munarini and an official match in which the red-and-white lineup remained in contention until the tiebreak. *Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/uyba-esordio-alla-pari-con-novara-al-tie-break-vince-la-igor/2698000/)*

item.title: Lido San Domenico: Lugano publishes two calls for tenders
item.description: The Municipal Council has launched the calls for tenders for the management of the refreshment bar and the renovation of the spaces through a public-private partnership.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Lugano City Council has published two tenders for the Lido - One concerns the buvette, the other its renovation - The choice will depend on the results of the two tenders - A petition has collected 4'000 signatures ## Key facts - Location: Lido San Domenico, Lugano - Buvette management: almost ten years with a longstanding duo - Deadline: in a few days - Partnership: public-private with an external investor - Petition: 4'000 signatures In Lugano, the Municipality has published two separate tenders for the future of Lido San Domenico, a historic city facility that risks changing its character. The tenders will close in a few days and have raised concerns among residents, artists and political representatives. One of the tenders concerns the new management of the buvette, which has remained in the hands of a longstanding duo for almost ten years. The other involves renovating the spaces through a possible public-private partnership with an external investor. It is precisely this prospect that has led many to fear a transformation of what the Lido offers, as it is considered much more than a simple bathing facility. Nina Pusterla, group leader of the Socialist Party in the Municipal Council, linked the discussion to the risk of losing, within Lugano’s urban fabric, a free place accessible to everyone and capable of fostering social interaction. The facility has also hosted musical, artistic and cultural initiatives. Pusterla raised these concerns in an interpellation to the Municipality, of which she is the first signatory. The text was also signed by representatives of other parties. ### The choice left open by the Municipality Roberto Badaracco, deputy mayor of Lugano, explained that the Municipality wanted to retain complete freedom of choice. Based on the results of the tenders, it will assess how many people will participate solely for the management and how many investors will be ready to step in. The reason given for the tender aimed at investors is the City’s financial situation: if an external party provides assistance through a public-private partnership, Lugano would save the sums required. The Municipality will therefore decide which of the two tenders to prioritize and cancel the other. The procedure follows a mobilization that took place two years ago, when protests persuaded the City to extend the concession to the current management. The future of Lido San Domenico is now once again at the center of public debate, just as the two tenders are approaching their closing date. ## The cultural role of the Lido The debate over Lido San Domenico has broadened to include the role the facility plays in city life. For many residents of Lugano, and not only them, the Lido is a place to have a drink, eat or relax, but also to exchange views and think about new projects. The discussion therefore concerns the possibility of preserving a gathering space connected to independent culture, in addition to its function as a bathing facility. A discussion was held at the Lido about the future of the spaces where independent culture can express itself. Artists, ordinary citizens and politicians came together to ask the City to review the plans that envisage a change in management. The initiative gave public expression to a concern already present in the debate over the two calls for tenders. ### The public and artists in the same place Leo Pusterla, a musician, described the role played by the Lido in the development of new initiatives. In his view, the facility managed to broaden the horizons of its programming and, at the same time, create a meeting place for the public and artists. He explained that this coexistence would have encouraged the emergence of new projects. Nina Pusterla instead emphasized the consequences of possible management driven above all by commercial considerations. She acknowledged that the economic situation is not easy, but argued that Lugano decides where to invest its resources. The concern expressed is that a public mandate of this kind would attract the usual suspects, but also different actors, according to commercial logic and economic spin-off considerations. Roberto Badaracco acknowledged that the place has a segment of the population that appreciates it precisely for what it offers. > «there is nevertheless a segment of the population that loves this place, also for what it offers. So in my opinion this should be protected.» The deputy mayor added that, in the Municipal Council's assessment, economic issues and profit should not be the only factors taken into account, because that would be a shame. He clarified that the decision also involves the other members of the executive. The discussion became intertwined with the announced closure of the L'Ove venue. In Lugano, therefore, demand for places to meet and develop initiatives is growing as some spaces disappear. Badaracco reported that the issue has been addressed for many years, but also stressed the difficulty of finding venues and reaching consensus within the Municipal Council, including among the different political forces. ## The next stages of the debate The closest step is the conclusion of the two competitions, scheduled in a few days. It will be on the basis of the results that the Municipality of Lugano will determine which path to prioritize for Lido San Domenico. The other competition will be cancelled, according to the municipal executive. The source does not yet indicate which of the two options will prevail. ### The request to review the calls The petition submitted in support of the Lido has collected 4'000 signatures. This is the second time that the future of the facility has received the support of citizens: the first mobilization mentioned in the source dates back to 2024. For Nina Pusterla, the main request is to review the two competitions. The Socialist party member first questioned the decision to separate them. She also indicated as particularly relevant the ten-year competition that calls for private parties to be involved in planning the renovation of the Lido. According to Pusterla, it is unclear why this step was entrusted to outside parties and why the City did not choose to invest its own resources. The debate does not, however, end with the petition. Within the Lido, independent culture continues to call for spaces in which it can express itself. Olmo Cerri, of the Idra association, spoke of many promises and ideas, but stressed that there is still no one willing to take concrete responsibility for making spaces available. In his assessment, there are intentions, but not yet anything concrete. The solutions being worked on include the new part of the former slaughterhouse and the former tailoring school. The source does not detail the role these places might play, but places them among the options being considered in response to the request for spaces. The future of the Lido thus remains tied to two decisions: the outcome of the competitions and the direction the Municipality will give to the management and renovation of the facility. In the meantime, the petition and the public debate keep open the request to protect a place associated with independent culture and civic social gathering. *Source: [rsi.ch](https://www.rsi.ch/s/4133115)*

item.title: Ticino health tax for cross-border workers: starting in September?
item.description: New healthcare tax for cross-border workers: launch expected by September, but implementing decrees are missing and payments have not yet been collected.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - It concerns some workers in border municipalities. - The administrative machinery should get underway by September. - Requests will follow regional procedures. - Payments have not yet been collected. ## Key facts - Start → by September - Eligible group → residents in Italy, employed in Switzerland and covered by the National Health Service - Calculation → percentage of income, with a minimum and maximum threshold - Regions → Lombardy and Piedmont among the first affected - Status → final implementing decrees still missing By September, the administrative machinery for the health tax intended for some workers who live in border municipalities and work in Switzerland should get underway. The contribution is at the center of discussions between Rome, the Regions and the Swiss authorities: the stated aim is to cover the costs of healthcare provided in Italy to those who earn their income across the border. The measure is part of the new tax relations between Italy and Switzerland, following the entry into force of the agreement on cross-border workers and the rules approved in Rome. The contribution should support the Italian healthcare system, but the measure is not yet active: the final implementing decrees are missing and the payments have not yet been collected. ### Expected timeline The timeline is one of the points most closely followed by trade unions and border municipalities. The first payment requests, according to the indications circulated so far, should arrive after the procedures have been finalized by the Regions concerned, starting with Lombardy and Piedmont, where a large proportion of the workers employed in Ticino live. This would not be a direct deduction from the Swiss payslip, but a contribution requested by the Italian authorities. For the cross-border worker, therefore, the difference concerns the channel through which any request would arrive, not just the name of the measure. To explore this distinction further, simulatore busta paga can be used alongside official communications, without turning it into a calculation of the amount owed. The scope has not yet been defined in every detail. The available reconstructions include workers resident in Italy who work in Switzerland and continue to use the National Health Service, while paying taxes or contributions partly across the border. In particular, the rules for old and new cross-border workers remain to be clarified, a distinction that is already central to the tax agreement between the two countries. > “Clarity is needed before sending payment notices,” explained a border trade-union representative. The representative recalled that many workers have already requested information from tax-assistance offices in Varese, Como and Verbano-Cusio-Ossola. For now, the picture points to a start expected by September and the involvement of local administrations; the definitive schedule for the requests and uniform procedures for all areas, however, are not yet in operation. For the cross-border worker residing in Italy, the first practical effect is not yet a figure to include in the household budget, but the impossibility of calculating it with the information available. The source indicates a percentage of income and a minimum and maximum threshold; however, it does not indicate the rates or establish whether the base will be net income or taxable income. The drafts and technical discussions considered both hypotheses, without reaching a rule that is the same for all territories. ### The variables that change the interpretation | Profile or variable | Available information | |---|---| | Residence and work | Italy and Switzerland, with use of the National Health Service | | Old or new cross-border worker | Distinction still to be clarified | | Calculation base | Net income or taxable income, according to the hypotheses discussed | | Amount | Percentage with a minimum and maximum threshold | | Non-payment | Question still open among workers | The contrast with the previous situation is clear: today the measure is not active and no payments have been collected; after its launch, however, the worker would have to deal with an Italian charge separate from the Swiss payslip. It is not yet possible to know whether the rules will be identical from one Region to another, because the text refers to regional procedures and non-uniform criteria. For families, the sensitive point is purchasing power. Italian border municipalities fear that a new levy could add to the difficulties already indicated: exchange rates, transport and price increases. The text does not quantify this pressure and therefore does not allow it to be converted into a monthly amount. A comparison on costo della vita Ticino vs Italia may help separate the impact of the measure from the other items mentioned, without attributing to the tax an amount that is still unavailable. In Canton Ticino, the authorities are following the dossier closely because any intervention concerning cross-border workers may affect the cantonal labor market. The source indicates sectors such as construction, healthcare, catering, logistics and services, where Italian labor remains important. The possible effect, therefore, does not concern only those who will receive a payment request: the comparison also involves relations between the territories. The subsequent steps also remain open. The trade unions are asking for uniform criteria and clear deadlines; the patronati are preparing for a phase that could generate confusion, especially in the small municipalities in the border area. If the letters arrived before the explanations, objections and appeals could be launched. The source does not, however, establish what the consequences of non-payment would be: this too is an answer that will have to come from the final rules. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. To deal with the phase preceding activation, the cross-border worker can follow a sequence limited to the information that has already emerged. The starting point is not an amount, but the procedure: the administrative launch is expected by September, while the first requests are linked to the completion of the regional steps. As long as the final implementing decrees are missing, there is no record of payments having already been collected. ### Five operational steps - Follow communications from the Regions concerned. Lombardy and Piedmont are indicated as the first areas for fine-tuning the procedures. - Identify the sender. Any request would come from the Italian authorities and not be a direct deduction from the Swiss payslip. - Read the scope applied. Residence in Italy, work in Switzerland, and use of the National Health Service are the elements cited to identify the workers involved. - Check the announced criteria. The distinction between existing and new cross-border workers, the basis of net income versus taxable income, and the minimum and maximum thresholds still need to be clarified. - Turn to patronage offices or trade unions for the questions that remain open: how much will be paid, from when, and what happens to those who do not pay. These steps do not replace a regional procedure: they serve to avoid confusing the stages. The source does not indicate a precise date for the first letters or an already operational schedule. Therefore, a communication arriving before the explanations would be exactly the case that unions and administrators fear: the criteria must be the same and the timing certain. The work expected of the Regions should cross-reference residence, income earned in Switzerland, and healthcare status in Italy. The verification may be complex because contracts, cantons of employment, length of employment, insurance coverage, and family circumstances vary. The practical point to keep distinct is that the group concerned is not described as homogeneous: the request may depend on the conditions that will be set by the competent administrations. If a problem were to emerge from the first request, the source does not rule out challenges and appeals. The patronage offices are preparing to handle this phase, especially in small border municipalities. The consequences of non-payment, however, have not been defined, so they should not be presented as already established. The person involved is a woman, who reportedly sustained moderately serious injuries. The initial information gathered at the scene by Rescue Media describes a loss of control while the vehicle was negotiating a bend.
For reasons yet to be established, the vehicle left the road and violently hit a traffic divider. The impact caused the car to overturn, and it came to rest on its roof. The account available in the initial reconstructions stops at these elements: the reason for the loss of control is not indicated.
The southbound motorway entrance was closed by the cantonal police. The measure affected access to the A2 at the point where operations were taking place. The woman was extracted from the vehicle and stabilized before being transferred to the emergency department of Ospedale Civico di Lugano.
The closure was maintained for over an hour to facilitate rescue operations and the recovery of the car. The case therefore combines the reconstruction of the vehicle leaving the road with the activities carried out at the interchange and the subsequent medical care provided to the injured woman. ## Rescue operations at the scene

item.title: Italy are world champions in blind baseball
item.description: Italy triumphs in Castiglione della Pescaia: Cuba defeated 10-4. Varese players Oliveri (MVP) and Trombini (best young player) were the protagonists.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Italy world champions in Castiglione della Pescaia - Cuba defeated 10-4 in the sixth inning - Danny Oliveri MVP, Fabio Trombini best young player - Vuolo and Boscardi on the Italian staff
## Key facts - Event → Blind Baseball International Cup - Location → Castiglione della Pescaia - Final → Italy-Cuba 10-4 - Manager → Marco Corazza - MVP → Danny Oliveri - Best young player → Fabio Trombini - Coaches → Francesco Vuolo and Matteo Boscardi - Batting → Danny Oliveri 5 for 7
Castiglione della Pescaia hosted the final of the Blind Baseball International Cup, which ended with the world title for Italy. The Azzurri, led by manager Marco Corazza, defeated Cuba 10-4, reaching the final result in the sixth inning. The game concluded a tournament characterized by outstanding performances and strong representation from the Varese area.
### A victory with roots in Varese
The Italian success indeed puts several figures linked to the province of Varese in the spotlight. Among the coaches of the Italian team were Francesco Vuolo and Matteo Boscardi, identified as coaches from Varese and as pillars of the local and national movement. The area’s presence did not stop at the bench, but also involved the protagonists on the field.
Fabio Trombini, a player for Hurricane Cisv Saronno, was among the most important performers in the competition. Alongside him, Danny Oliveri, a Varese resident by adoption and former Hurricane player, stood out. Oliveri finished the tournament 5 for 7 at bat and was named MVP of the event.
The recognition awarded to Trombini was that of best young player of the entire World Championship. The Italian team thus collected results and individual awards, with the contribution from Varese distributed between the technical leadership and the field. The title won against Cuba represents the culmination of this journey, but the story of the victory also includes the roles held by the protagonists linked to Varese and Saronno. ## The Azzurri's journey
### The results from the first phase
Before the final, Italy had built its path with three clear wins in the tournament's opening phase. The results reported by the competition are these:
| Phase | Opponent | Result | |---|---|---| | First phase | Olanda | 20-0 | | First phase | Chinese Taipei | 8-0 | | First phase | Pakistan | 15-1 |
The performance in the first part took the Azzurri into the knockout matches. Here the team had to confirm what it had shown in the previous games, facing opponents at a stage with no room for mistakes. In the semifinal, Italy overcame Great Britain 11-4, securing access to the final against Cuba.
### The sequence of the final
The title game began uphill. In the second inning, Cuba took a 1-0 lead after a defensive mistake by Italy. In the third inning, however, the Azzurri turned the situation around by scoring three runs with two outs. The reaction did not end the game: in the fourth inning, the Cuban team regained the lead, moving ahead 4-3.
The turning point came in the fifth inning. Italy took advantage of four hits and two errors by the opponents to put together a five-run inning. The score thus moved to 8-4, creating the decisive margin in the closing part of the game.
In the sixth inning, the Azzurri added two more runs, reaching the final score of 10-4. A defensive double play closed out the game. The progression of the game shows the shift from the initial deficit to the comeback, and finally the breakaway that gave Italy the world blind baseball title. ## The Varese-area contribution to the title
### Bench and field
The local character of the victory emerges from the makeup of the Italian contingent. The Varese area is represented both in the coaching staff and among the players who received the tournament's main individual awards. The two Varese coaches, Francesco Vuolo and Matteo Boscardi, worked from the bench, described as fundamental guides for the team and pillars of the local and national movement.
On the field, the key figure is Danny Oliveri. The player, who made Varese his home and is a former Hurricane, was one of the competition's standout performers. His performance is summed up by his 5-for-7 at the plate, while the MVP award named him the best player in the tournament.
### Individual awards
Alongside Oliveri, the event also honored Fabio Trombini. The Hurricane Cisv Saronno player was recognized as the best young player of the entire World Championship. The two awards highlight two different aspects of Italy's performance: on the one hand, the impact of a player named MVP; on the other, the emergence of a young player from the Saronno team.
The Varese-area tally therefore includes two coaches, an MVP and the competition's best young player. This is not merely a numerical presence in the contingent, but roles and results explicitly highlighted in the account of the tournament. The bench led by Vuolo and Boscardi, Oliveri's performance and the recognition earned by Trombini together form the local dimension of the success.
With the title won in Castiglione della Pescaia, Italy concludes a tournament in which the Varese contribution was visible in every decisive area: in the team's leadership, on-field performance and the awards presented at the end of the competition.

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Mobilization on Friday 9 October at 14 - Meeting point at Eremo di Miazzina - Work, care and families at the center
- What: trade union mobilization - When: Friday 9 October, at 14 - Where: Eremo di Miazzina - Promoters: Cgil Novara Vco, Cisl Piemonte Orientale and Uil Novara Vco - Themes: work, assistance and support for families
### The call The meeting promoted by Cgil Novara Vco, Cisl Piemonte Orientale and Uil Novara Vco, together with their respective Funzione Pubblica categories, is scheduled at Eremo di Miazzina on Friday 9 October at 14. The organizations have announced the mobilization, identifying three related themes: work, assistance and support for families.
The message chosen to present the initiative places respect for those who work, those receiving care and families at the center. > “We ask for respect: for those who work, for those receiving care, for families.”
The unions explain that respect for rights must not remain a statement of principle. In their view, it must translate into concrete choices, responsibilities and commitments on everyone’s part. The mobilization is therefore described as a call for attention directed at different people and stakeholders.
### The demands For those who work, the demand calls for dignity, safety and protections. For people who need care and assistance, it calls for answers. For families who care every day for those who are most vulnerable, it asks for support.
The appeal also involves institutions, politics and employers. Among other commitments, the organizations ask the latter to guarantee wages currently unpaid, decent working conditions, safety and stability. Greater attention to reconciling private and professional life is also called for.
To politicians, however, the statement asks that commitments be transformed into decisions, resources and services capable of affecting people’s lives, preventing them from remaining merely announcements. The stated objective is not to create divisions: the unions want to involve everyone who has a responsibility in building a fairer society.
The statement is signed by general secretaries Michele Piffero for Cgil Novara Vco, Elena Ugazio for Cisl Piemonte Orientale and Stefano De Grandis for Uil Novara Vco, together with representatives of their respective Funzione Pubblica categories. The choice of 9 October is presented as the way to bring work, care and families back to the same table, considered parts of the same community and its future. ### Three levels of the mobilization The practical reading of the statement starts with the allocation of responsibilities. There is not a single undifferentiated request: the text separates the needs of those who work, those who need care and assistance, and families who look after the most vulnerable people. At the same time, it distinguishes what is being asked of employers from what is being asked of policymakers.
| Scope | Request contained in the statement | |---|---| | Work | dignity, safety, protections, wages unpaid to date and stability | | Care | responses for those who need care and assistance | | Families | support and attention to reconciling private and professional life |
This distinction provides a first criterion for interpreting the appeal. For workers, the issue of unpaid wages is accompanied by requests concerning the quality of working conditions, safety and stability. The statement does not indicate amounts, periods or individual positions: it therefore does not make it possible to reconstruct individual cases.
In terms of care, the request concerns responses for people who need assistance. No specific services or operating procedures are indicated. For families too, the text expresses a specific need, support, but does not describe a particular procedure or measure.
The distinction also concerns the parties addressed. Employers are asked to take action on wages and conditions; policymakers are asked to turn commitments into decisions, resources and services. Responsibilities are therefore not conflated, but assigned to different actors.
The informational limitation is clear: the source announces a mobilization and sets out its demands, but does not introduce new rules or indicate individual procedures. For a separate in-depth analysis focusing solely on the pay-related topic, simulatore busta paga is available.

2. Separate the three themes. The mobilization concerns work, assistance and support for families. Distinguishing these areas makes it possible to read the requests without turning them into a single indistinct demand.

item.title: Tre Valli Varesine, the history on display at Le Corti
item.description: Twenty panels retrace at the Corti di Varese the history of the Tre Valli Varesine from 1919 to the present day. Exhibition until October 20.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Twenty panels tell the story of the Tre Valli from 1919 to the present day - The exhibition is at Le Corti di Varese until Tuesday 20 October - A 231-page volume with 320 photographs was announced
## Key facts - Location → Centro Commerciale Le Corti di Varese, basement level two - Curator → Sergio Gianoli - Promoter → Ciclovarese - Collaboration → Gandini Activ Group - Exhibition → 20 panels - Period covered → from 1919 to modern times - Visit → until Tuesday 20 October, during opening hours - Volume → 231 pages and 320 photographs
### The exhibition on basement level two Centro Commerciale Le Corti di Varese is hosting, on basement level two, the exhibition dedicated to the history of the Tre Valli Varesine. The official inauguration took place yesterday morning, with an exhibition organized by Ciclovarese, set up in collaboration with Gandini Activ Group and curated by Sergio Gianoli.
The exhibition brings together twenty panels. The panels feature photographs and commentary on the most significant editions of the classic cycling race in Varese, spanning from 1919 to modern times. The exhibition is therefore dedicated to telling, through images and words, the story of more than a century of cycling in Varese, following the approach announced for the exhibition.
The exhibition can be visited during the opening hours of Centro Commerciale Le Corti until Tuesday 20 October. The venue indicated for the visit is basement level two, the same space where the official inauguration took place. The panels will remain available beyond the opening morning, in line with the period indicated for the exhibition.
The presentation also had a second outcome: during the morning in Varese, the second edition of the volume Tre Valli Varesine – la storia was announced. The publication will retrace all the editions of the race, according to what was communicated during the inauguration. ## The volume and the historical arc The second edition of Tre Valli Varesine – la storia was announced during the morning at Centro Commerciale Le Corti. The source attributes a precise objective to the book: retrace all the editions of the classic cycling race from Varese, including both the men's and women's races.
The editorial project will also include the race on the upcoming 6 October. The reference to the upcoming edition of the race appears alongside the historical reconstruction, which spans from the first editions in 1919 to modern times. The second edition is described as a work devoted to all the men's and women's editions.
### Publication data | Element | Data | |---|---| | Pages | 231 | | Photographs | 320 | | Images | Some previously unpublished | | Publisher | SunriseMedia |
The announced figures define the publishing project: 231 pages and 320 photographs, with some previously unpublished images. The publisher indicated is SunriseMedia. The exhibition, on the other hand, brings the material together in twenty panels with photographs and commentary on the most significant Tre Valli Varesine.
The distinction between the two formats is explicit in the presentation. On the one hand, there are the panels displayed at Le Corti; on the other, the volume that will retrace all the editions of the race, including the men's and women's competitions. The source thus connects the entire history of the Varese competition to the announced publishing project. ## The upcoming dates The continuation of the initiative is marked by three time references indicated in the news. The exhibition remains open to visitors until Tuesday 20 October; it can be visited during the opening hours of Centro Commerciale Le Corti, and the indicated location is level minus two. The end date concerns the exhibition inaugurated yesterday morning in Varese.
Before the exhibition closes, the publishing project refers to the race on the upcoming 6 October. The second edition of the volume Tre Valli Varesine – la storia will in fact also include that race, within the account of all the editions of the race, men's and women's. The date of 6 October is therefore the sporting date mentioned in the presentation of the book.
### The sale of the volume The next step is scheduled for the second half of next month, November. From that moment, according to the announcement, the volume will be on sale. The publication will be published by SunriseMedia, and the source presents it as the second edition of the book devoted to the history of Tre Valli Varesine.
The sequence communicated is this: the exhibition remains at Le Corti until Tuesday 20 October, the race on the upcoming 6 October enters the publishing reconstruction, and the book goes on sale in the second half of November. The opening hours remain those of Centro Commerciale Le Corti. These are the stages indicated for the continuation of the initiative and for the announced commercial availability of the volume.

item.title: Saracino, new commander of the Carabinieri in Mornago
item.description: Lieutenant with Special Charge Anacleto Antonio Saracino leads the Carabinieri Station of Mornago, under the Gallarate Company, responsible for public safety in the municipalities of Mornago, Sumirago, Casale Litta and Inarzo.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Saracino leads the Mornago Station - The station covers four municipalities - De Vico received him this morning - His career in the Carabinieri began in 1991
## Key facts - New commander → Special Assignment Lieutenant Anacleto Antonio Saracino - Station → Mornago Carabinieri Station - Reporting line → Gallarate Company - Municipalities → Mornago, Sumirago, Casale Litta and Inarzo - Provincial commander → Colonel Alessandro De Vico - Duties → Public security and territorial control
Special Assignment Lieutenant Anacleto Antonio Saracino is the new Commander of the Mornago Carabinieri Station. This morning, the officer was received by Colonel Alessandro De Vico, Provincial Commander of the Carabinieri in Varese. The provincial commander extended his greetings and wished him success in his work for the new institutional mission leading the local station.
### The station and the new responsibility
The Mornago Carabinieri Station falls under the Gallarate Company and represents a local station of fundamental strategic importance. The Carabinieri command’s primary task is to oversee public security and territorial control.
The station’s activities concern the residents of four communities: Mornago, Sumirago, Casale Litta and Inarzo. The command’s area of responsibility is therefore not limited to the municipality in which the station is located, but includes the four communities indicated in the source.
Saracino’s reception by the Provincial Commander marks the beginning of his new institutional mission. De Vico’s greetings and good wishes are connected to his taking charge of the station, while its placement under the Gallarate Company defines the structure in which the Mornago Station operates. The report thus presents a local assignment with a precise scope: one station, a chain of command and four communities entrusted to the station for public security and territorial control functions. This is the framework of the new command indicated by the source. ## From Puglia to Lombardy
The new commander takes up the position after a career in the Carabinieri that began in the province of Lecce. Saracino is originally from that area and began his professional experience in 1991, when he was just over twenty years old.
### The first stages in the Carabinieri
The first training listed in his service history is the 161st Auxiliary Carabinieri Course, attended at the Carabinieri Cadet School in Chieti. After completing the course, Saracino was assigned to the 11th Carabinieri Battalion in Bari. These were the initial stages of the career that took him from Puglia to his subsequent experience in Lombardy.
At the end of the 47th Non-Commissioned Officers Cadet Course, the NCO in fact arrived in Lombardy. His first two years of service in the region took place in Milan, at the 3rd Lombardy Carabinieri Battalion. The source therefore places the move to a new area of service during this phase, after the experience gained in Bari.
In 1999, he was transferred to the Carnago Carabinieri Station. Saracino served in that unit for more than twenty years. This represents the longest part of the career described in the source and links his name to a prolonged presence at a Carabinieri station in the province of Varese.
The professional sequence thus includes the start in 1991, training in Chieti, assignment to Bari, the two years in Milan and the long period spent in Carnago. Each step is identified as part of the career preceding his current responsibility in Mornago. The reconstruction lists the locations and courses mentioned in the source without adding any other assignments or stages beyond those documented. ## The new role in Mornago
The most recent phase of Saracino's career took place at the same Station he is now called upon to lead. In 2023, he was assigned to the Mornago Carabinieri Station, where to date he has held the role of subordinate non-commissioned officer.
### The succession of assignments
| Period | Step indicated by the source | |---|---| | 2023 | Assignment to the Mornago Carabinieri Station | | To date | Service as a subordinate non-commissioned officer | | New appointment | Official leadership of the Station as Commander |
The transition to leading the station thus comes after a period of service already completed in Mornago. The source describes this development as a path of continuity in the area: the 2023 assignment and the work as a subordinate non-commissioned officer directly precede the assumption of command.
The central point of what follows is the transformation of the role held at the station. Saracino is not presented merely as the service member assigned to a new station, but as the non-commissioned officer who, after serving in Mornago, now assumes its official leadership. This is the succession indicated: first the assignment to the location, then the work as a subordinate non-commissioned officer, and finally the new appointment as Commander.
The new responsibility thus closes the part of the career described in the source relating to his time in Mornago and opens the institutional mission of leading the station. His previous service at the station and the command just assumed are linked by the continuity in the area referred to in the article. For local reporting, the documented transition is therefore from a subordinate role to official responsibility for the Mornago Carabinieri Station.

item.title: Nighttime accident in Gallarate: three young people involved
item.description: Accident in Gallarate, on Stelvio: three young people aged 18, 20 and 24 involved. Two were transported to the hospitals of Legnano and Gallarate.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Car collision shortly after 4 on via Stelvio - Three young people aged 18, 20 and 24 involved - Two taken to the hospitals in Legnano and Gallarate - Red code later downgraded to yellow
## Key facts - Location → via Stelvio, Gallarate - Time → shortly after 4 - Involved → 18, 20 and 24 years old - Emergency response → red code, then yellow - Transfers → hospitals in Legnano and Gallarate
### The accident on via Stelvio Shortly after 4, on via Stelvio in Gallarate, a car collision required emergency responders to assist three young people. Ambulances rushed to youths aged 18, 20 and 24, while the response had been classified as a red code.
Subsequently, the youths appeared to be in less serious condition and the code was downgraded to yellow. Two of the three were taken to the hospitals in Legnano and Gallarate. The source names the two facilities, but does not associate each young person with a specific hospital.
The incident took place at night and the location given is via Stelvio. As for how it happened, the report mentions a car collision and adds no other details. It does, however, specify the approximate time, shortly after 4, the ages of the three people involved, the sequence of the emergency code, and the transfer of two people.
The report therefore describes a response that began as a red code and was then downgraded to yellow. The update on their condition indicates a situation that appeared less serious, but does not change the essential facts: three youths involved and two hospital transports. The article provides no further individual details about the youths. ## The picture of the night
### The reported incidents The case on via Stelvio fits into a night that, according to the report, had no other major incidents, except for an incident in Vedano shortly after midnight. The distinction is clear: on the one hand, the collision between cars in Gallarate, on the other, the incident recorded in Vedano.
In Vedano, the source reports a car hitting an obstacle and assistance being provided to a twenty-year-old. No other details about the incident are indicated; the reported information concerns the vehicle, the obstacle and the age of the person assisted.
That same night, assaults were also reported in Castiglione, Gallarate and Fagnano. The text specifies that the consequences were not serious. The three locations are mentioned together, but the source does not attribute them to a single incident: it presents them as separate reports, without indicating times or the number of people involved.
The list of interventions finally includes Caravate, where alcohol intoxication was reported. Here too, no details are added about the circumstances or the person's condition. The report is limited to the nature of the intervention and the location.
| Location | Reported intervention | |---|---| | Vedano | Car hitting an obstacle and assistance provided to a twenty-year-old | | Castiglione, Gallarate and Fagnano | Assaults with non-serious consequences | | Caravate | Alcohol intoxication |
Overall, the source places alongside the Gallarate case a road incident in Vedano and other reports in the locations mentioned, without establishing connections between the interventions. ## The available update
### From red code to transport The follow-up explicitly reported for the accident in Gallarate concerns the assessment of the emergency and the transfers. The sequence starts with the response under a red code and continues with the downgrade to yellow, after the young people's conditions appeared less serious. This is the step that updates the initial picture.
Operationally, two of the three young people were transported to the hospitals of Legnano and Gallarate. The report keeps separate the number of people involved from the number transported: three young people were involved, while two transfers are indicated. It does not specify which young person was taken to each facility, and no further individual updates are reported.
The source does not add a more detailed account of the collision between cars. Nor does it indicate any further developments for the others involved, or any other communications about the hospitals. For the case of Vedano, the assaults reported in Castiglione, Gallarate and Fagnano, and the alcohol intoxication in Caravate, the text goes no further than the interventions described during the night.
The picture conveyed by the news therefore stops at the elements reported: the accident on Via Stelvio shortly after 4, the ages of the three young people, the change from red code to yellow and the two transports to the hospitals of Legnano and Gallarate. No further steps are announced in the available report.

item.title: Cecco Vescovi: Della Valle is the key man for Openjobmetis
item.description: Cecco Vescovi, a guest on «Luci a Masnago», analyzed the defeat suffered by Openjobmetis Varese against Virtus Bologna, emphasizing the absences and Della Valle's key role.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - «Luci a Masnago» analyzed the debut against Virtus Bologna - Vescovi identifies Della Valle as Varese's key player - Della Valle is set to miss Scafati and Murcia - The game against Bologna drew 5.394 spectators
## Key facts - Program → «Luci a Masnago» - Broadcaster → Radio Materia - Guest → Cecco Vescovi - Opponent → Virtus Bologna - Absences → McDowell White and Amedeo Della Valle - Attendance → 5.394 spectators - Next opponent → Longobardi Scafati - European debut → Murcia, Basketball Champions League
Openjobmetis Varese's home debut against Virtus Bologna, at the Masnago sports hall, opened the second season of «Luci a Masnago» with a false start. The final result left a bitter taste, but the program also scrutinized the way the game unfolded.
The first episode of the second season of the Radio Materia program, hosted by Damiano Franzetti, Francesco Brezzi and Luca Antonelli, was dedicated to the clash with the Bologna side and the difficulties shown by the red-and-white team. The special guest was Cecco Vescovi, the record-holder for appearances in Pallacanestro Varese's history, winner of the 1999 scudetto and now general manager of GEAS Sesto San Giovanni, a team in the top women's league.
Vescovi took part in the discussion about the current Openjobmetis, also recalling his long red-and-white past and his connection with the Masnago sports hall.
### Assessing the debut
In the technical analysis, the starting point was Virtus's physicality and the approach with which Bologna played the game. According to Vescovi, these elements exposed Varese's structural difficulties, as the team took the court without McDowell White and Amedeo Della Valle.
The two absences were considered particularly significant because they concern the positions from which all the play begins. Vescovi identified Virtus as the worst opponent to face on the first day of the season because of the type of basketball played by Openjobmetis: both teams like to play at speed, but Bologna was more accustomed to responding to that volume of play. Against another team capable of maintaining a more normal pace, the impact could have been different.
The discussion focused above all on Della Valle, the player around whom the team was built. Vescovi described him as follows:
> «He is far too important an addition to do without: he is an incredible impact player who produces for himself and others, drawing the defense and creating space.»
His return, together with that of McDowell White, is considered crucial when Varese needs to slow down, change pace or reverse unfavorable momentum. Della Valle can draw a foul, go to the free-throw line, run the pick-and-roll and help the team think. When the game proceeds at a gallop throughout, however, the risk Vescovi identified is that of absorbing pressure without managing to regain control of the game. The most personal segment of the episode concerned the bond between Cecco Vescovi and the Masnago sports hall. As a player born and raised in Varese, the former red-and-white player retraced his long relationship with the Pallacanestro Varese environment and linked those memories to the situation of the current captain.
The recipient of the advice was Matteo Librizzi, also from Varese and now the team captain. Vescovi suggested that he not stop at the level he had reached and not settle for what he currently had. The advice was to always seek new avenues for his game and remain committed to improving at every opportunity.
The reasoning starts from familiarity with the place where one grew up. Playing at home is comfortable, but that very comfort can lead one to sit back, that is, to stop looking for new room for improvement. Vescovi acknowledged having made the same mistake when he was young and hoped that Librizzi would not repeat that path. The message addressed to the captain therefore concerns personal and technical growth, beyond simply performing in the next game.
### The other topics of the program
The episode did not focus solely on the men's team. Women's basketball was also discussed during the program, with the new feature curated by Marco Pinti. The broadcast also analyzed the red-and-whites' next opponent, Longobardi Scafati, placing the upcoming game within the context of the issues left open after the debut.
There was also room for the Masnago venue, which had shown some organizational problems during the game against Virtus. The attendance figure was nevertheless significant: 5.394 spectators were recorded in the stands.
The number was mentioned during the brief segment dedicated to the arena, together with the difficulties that emerged during the first home game. The attention paid to the venue concerned not only the organization of the game, but also the elements that shape the spectators' experience. The audio was identified as a traditional Achilles' heel of the facility, while the lighting was included among the aspects set to improve.
The subject of the arena thus stood alongside the technical aspect and the one linked to the red-and-white history. On the one hand, there was the analysis of absences and the pace of the game; on the other, Vescovi's relationship with Masnago and the advice addressed to Librizzi; in between, the content dedicated to women's basketball, the next game and the condition of the venue.
The broadcast therefore brought together commentary on the debut, the memory of Pallacanestro Varese and updates on the setting surrounding the team's games. For Openjobmetis, what comes next, as outlined in the episode, is marked by the upcoming fixtures and the situation of the two injured players. Pallacanestro Varese is keeping information about McDowell White confidential: the extent of his muscular problem is not known exactly.
Amedeo Della Valle, meanwhile, is still working separately. The reported forecast is that he will almost certainly be absent on Sunday in Scafati and on Wednesday in Murcia, where the team playing under the Itelyum brand will make its Basketball Champions League debut.
The first game on the schedule is against Longobardi Scafati, scheduled for Sunday 4 at 17. For Varese, this is the next step after the home debut against Virtus, but the outlook for the game remains tied to the availability of the two players mentioned during the broadcast.
The second fixture is in Murcia, where the Itelyum-branded team is set to make its European debut. The gap between the two fixtures was highlighted together with Della Valle's probable absence, as he continues to work separately. For McDowell White, meanwhile, the muscular problem remains without a precise assessment reported in the episode.
Meanwhile, an old friend of Varese has changed teams: Bryant Dunston has signed with Olympiacos. The news was mentioned in the part dedicated to Europe, alongside the team's imminent debut in Basketball Champions League.
As for the arena, starting with the next game, both the sound system and the lighting should improve significantly, if everything goes smoothly. The stated aim is to fix the long-standing sound problem and make the atmosphere at the game more intense for the fans.
With the start of the league, «Dal Parquet» also returned to the air, the VareseNews podcast that comments on all Openjobmetis games. The first episode is available in the dedicated box and on listening platforms. This is the content accompanying the new phase of the season, as the team prepares for the games in Scafati and Murcia and awaits more precise updates on the injured players.

item.description: The Marcello Morandini Foundation of Varese is offering four events in October 2026, including visits, a concert, a catalogue and a workshop, accompanying the exhibition 'Antonio Barrese: Morphologies of Light' open until December 20, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Four events accompany the exhibition in October - Children's tour, concert, catalogue and creative workshop - The exhibition remains open until 20 December 2026
## Key facts - Exhibition → «Antonio Barrese: Morphologies of Light» - Venue → Fondazione Marcello Morandini, Varese - Children's tour → Saturday 3 October, at 15.30 - Concert → Sunday 4 October, at 11 - Conference → Friday 9 October, at 18.30 - Kids Lab → Saturday 24 October, at 15.30
On Saturday 3 October at 15.30, Fondazione Marcello Morandini in Varese will host the first event in the cultural programme accompanying the exhibition «Antonio Barrese: Morphologies of Light». The event is a guided tour for children aged 6 and over, led by Antonio Barrese himself and curator Stefania Gaudiosi.
The youngest visitors will discover the exhibition's works and themes through a tour designed to stimulate curiosity and creativity. The tour launches a schedule consisting of four events, organised in October for audiences of different ages.
### The two events of the first weekend
The programme includes guided tours, a concert, a conference with the presentation of the catalogue and a workshop for children. Following Saturday's initiative, on Sunday 4 October at 11, music will return with the fifth concert of the «Sintonie» season.
The event will feature four double bass players from the Orchestra del Teatro alla Scala di Milano: Omar Lonati, Giorgio Magistroni, Claudio Nicotra and Alessandro Serra. The programme includes music by Giuseppe Verdi, Georges Bizet and Carlo Galante.
Carlo Galante himself will be present to introduce the concert and one of his own compositions, which will be performed for the first time. The musical portion thus forms part of the schedule of activities accompanying the exhibition in the spaces of Fondazione Marcello Morandini.
The two dates of the first weekend therefore offer different activities: the visit on 3 October takes children among the works and themes of the exhibition, while the concert on 4 October presents a programme dedicated to Verdi, Bizet and Galante, performed by four double bass players from the Orchestra del Teatro alla Scala.
The exhibition is curated by Stefania Gaudiosi and devoted to Antonio Barrese's research at the intersection of art, science and design. The exhibition will remain open in the spaces on via Del Cairo until 20 December 2026, while October's schedule will continue with the conference devoted to the catalogue and the creative workshop for younger visitors. On Friday 9 October at 18.30, the cultural program of Fondazione Marcello Morandini will enter the phase devoted to in-depth exploration. A conference is scheduled, with the participation of Antonio Barrese and Stefania Gaudiosi, curator of the exhibition «Antonio Barrese: Morphologies of Light».
The exhibition catalogue will also be presented during the meeting. The volume is the first catalogue of the Foundation curated directly by the artist and serves a dual function: an archival document and a tool for critical analysis.
### The catalogue as a document of the project
The publication brings together texts, images and materials related to the exhibition itinerary. It also includes documentation of the main activities carried out as part of the project. The presentation on 9 October will therefore bring together the two people responsible for the exhibition and guide the public through the contents collected in the volume.
The catalogue concerns an exhibition that retraces Barrese's research, founder and driving force behind Gruppo MID – Mutamento Immagine Dimensione – and, since the 1960s, a leading figure in a journey in which artistic experimentation, science and technology intertwine.
At the heart of the exhibition is light, studied as a formal and conceptual material. The exhibition also presents it as an element capable of generating and transforming space. The itinerary includes images and interactive works, with a selection of historical and recent works produced over a span of sixty years, from 1965 to 2025.
The installation also invites visitors to engage with the works and explore the possibilities of light as a language and form of expression. The exhibition project is therefore not limited to a succession of works: it also includes materials and activities gathered in the publication presented during the conference.
The curatorial work of Stefania Gaudiosi accompanies this reconstruction of Barrese's research, while the catalogue adds specific documentation on the exhibition itinerary and the main initiatives carried out by the Foundation. The conference on 9 October is the calendar event devoted to presenting this volume.
The exhibition is held under the patronage and with the support of Regione Lombardia, and under the patronage of Comune di Varese. The exhibition continues at Fondazione Marcello Morandini until 20 December 2026, with historical and recent works spanning the period from 1965 to 2025. Saturday 24 October at 15.30, the October calendar of Fondazione Marcello Morandini will conclude with the «Kids Lab». The workshop is aimed at girls and boys aged 3 to 10 and seeks to bring young people closer to art through play, experimentation and creativity.
This event completes the part of the program dedicated to children. The guided tour on 3 October is reserved for children aged 6 and over, while the workshop on 24 October is aimed at a broader age range, from 3 to 10 years. The two activities are therefore distinct in terms of age and approach: the first accompanies participants in discovering the works and themes of the exhibition, while the second uses play, experimentation and creativity to bring young people closer to art.
### The venue and opening hours
Fondazione Marcello Morandini is located at via Francesco Del Cairo 41 in Varese. The museum is open on Thursdays from 15 to 18 and from Friday to Sunday from 10 to 13 and from 14 to 18.
| Day | Hours | |---|---| | Thursday | 15-18 | | Friday to Sunday | 10-13 and 14-18 |
The venue at via Del Cairo hosts the exhibition «Antonio Barrese: Morfologie di luce», which will remain open to visitors until 20 December 2026. The month’s calendar concludes with the workshop on 24 October, following the children’s tour, the concert in the «Sintonie» season and the conference presenting the catalog.
Information about the exhibition, events and tickets is available on the website www.fondazionemarcellomorandini.com. The October program takes place within the exhibition curated by Stefania Gaudiosi, held under the patronage and with the contribution of Regione Lombardia and under the patronage of the Comune di Varese.
The «Kids Lab» is the final date listed for the month. With this activity, Fondazione proposes an event specifically dedicated to girls and boys, keeping the program connected to the themes of the exhibition and to the possibilities of light as a language and form of expression.

item.title: Busto Arsizio: license suspended for 15 days for assault
item.description: The Police Commissioner of Varese suspended the license of a bar in Busto Arsizio for 15 days after the September 20 assault involving stones being thrown near a couple with a stroller; the injured person was taken to the hospital in Gallarate.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - License suspended for 15 days by the Questore of Varese - Assault on the evening of 20 settembre in Busto Arsizio - Stones thrown near a couple with a stroller - Injured man taken to the hospital in Gallarate ## Key facts - Measure → suspension of the license for 15 days - Authority → Questore of Varese - Location → bar in Busto Arsizio - Intervention → State Police and Carabinieri - Incident → brawl, stone-throwing and assault - Injured man → taken to the hospital in Gallarate - Legal basis → Article 100 of the Tulps ### The decision after the assault The State Police notified the owner of a bar in Busto Arsizio of the measure by which the Questore of Varese ordered the suspension of the establishment’s license for 15 days. The decision was prompted by serious incidents that caused disturbances to public order and safety. The incident that led to the measure took place on the evening of 20 settembre. A State Police patrol car and a Carabinieri patrol intervened at the premises following a report of a brawl. When they arrived, the fight had already ended. The officers collected the testimonies of those present and reviewed the surveillance footage. The investigation established that shortly beforehand, a violent assault had taken place against a man. Some people had thrown stones at him, among other things putting at risk the safety of a passing couple with a stroller. Subsequently, one of the group members physically attacked the man, throwing him to the ground. Medical personnel had to intervene for the injured man. After providing initial aid, they took him to the hospital in Gallarate. The notification therefore concerns the license of an establishment in Busto Arsizio and follows the reconstruction of a sequence involving stone-throwing and physical assault, as well as the presence of passersby exposed to danger. The measure was communicated to the owner by the State Police. The duration set by the Questore of Varese is 15 days, with the stated reason being the protection of public order and safety. ## The Police Headquarters’ investigation The administrative inquiry began with a request from the Busto Arsizio Public Security Police Station. The report concerned in particular the serious incident of violence that took place at the venue and the intervention of law enforcement. The inquiry was subsequently conducted by the Administrative Police Division of the Varese Police Headquarters. The initial evidence was gathered during the intervention by the State Police patrol unit and the Carabinieri patrol. Although the fight had already ended, the officers heard statements from those present and viewed the surveillance footage. The checks brought to light what had happened shortly before the report, including the assault on the man and the danger created by stones being thrown near the couple with a stroller. The proceedings also refer to previous incidents concerning the same public establishment. According to the findings, the bar had previously been subject to similar licence suspension measures under Article 100 of the Consolidated Law on Public Security, the Tulps. ### Description of the clientele Again according to the findings, the venue reportedly represented a regular gathering place for people with police records and socially dangerous individuals. The source links this situation to a consequent exposure to risks to public order and safety. This element adds to the report by the Police Station and the reconstruction carried out by the Police Headquarters’ offices. The roles of the various offices are indicated separately: the Police Station reported the incident, the Division conducted the inquiry, and the Chief of Police ordered the suspension. The measure is based on the evidence gathered through the activities of the Administrative Police Division and on the seriousness of the incident. ## The follow-up to the measure The administrative follow-up described by the source is the notification to the bar owner of the decision adopted by the Police Commissioner of Varese. The State Police notified the measure ordering the suspension of the establishment's license for 15 days. The measure therefore concerns the public establishment in Busto Arsizio and has a defined duration. ### The basis for the decision The regulatory reference indicated is Article 100 of the Consolidated Text of Public Security Laws, the Tulps. The same provision is cited for the previous suspension measures already adopted against the public establishment. The source links the application of the article to the need to intervene after incidents that caused disturbances to public order and safety. The Police Commissioner of Varese ordered the suspension after considering the seriousness of the facts and the evidence collected. The stated purpose of the measure is to protect public order and citizens' safety. The order establishes a temporary suspension of the license, set at fifteen days, and links it to the protection of the community. The sequence of acts concludes with the notification carried out by the State Police to the owner. Before that came the request from the Busto Arsizio Public Security Police Station and the work of the Administrative Police Division of the Varese Police Headquarters; after assessing the evidence, the Police Commissioner adopted the measure provided for by Article 100 of the Tulps. The result reported by the source is a temporary suspension of the license, justified by the established violence and the risks identified for public order and safety. *Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/rissa-e-aggressione-con-lancio-di-pietre-la-questura-sospende-per-15-giorni-la-licenza-di-un-bar-di-busto-arsizio/2697139/)*
