item.title: At the MA*GA in Gallarate, the Contemporary Day
item.description: Saturday 10 October at the MA*GA Museum in Gallarate, free admission, closing event for three exhibitions, books, video and performance for the XXII Contemporary Day.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Saturday 10 October free admission to MA*GA - Three exhibitions reach the finissage - The programme starts at 4 p.m. with a video - At 6 p.m. ‘Until there’s no air’ closes
## Key facts - Location → MA*GA Museum, Gallarate - Occasion → XXII Contemporary Day AMACI - Date → Saturday 10 October - Admission → free all day - Programme start → 4 p.m. - Series → ‘i Quaderni – Italia 2050 Research Centre of the MA*GA Museum’ - Publisher → Nomos Edizioni - Final appointment → ‘Until there’s no air’ by Martina Rota
### Saturday’s programme
On Saturday 10 October the MA*GA Museum in Gallarate organises a programme dedicated to contemporary art on the occasion of the XXII Contemporary Day AMACI. The initiative proposes to encounter art through exhibitions, books, video and performance and coincides with the finissage of three exhibitions currently on display at the museum.
The exhibitions concerned are ‘Qui e altrove. The environments of Paolo Scheggi 1964–1971’, ‘Le strade terminano prima di cominciare. Vincenzo Agnetti and the photographic traces’ and ‘ARTE VIVA. Performative and participatory processes as practice – XXVIII Gallarate Prize’. Their titles recall the three nuclei indicated by the day: the environments of Paolo Scheggi, the photographic traces of Vincenzo Agnetti and the performative and participatory processes of the Gallarate Prize.
The programme therefore pairs the closing of the exhibitions with a calendar devoted to publishing, research and performative practices. A video screening, institutional greetings, the presentation of the series ‘i Quaderni – Italia 2050 Research Centre of the MA*GA Museum’, a performance and the presentation of a catalogue are scheduled. The full timetable is indicated in the day’s programme.
Access to the MA*GA Museum will be free all day. It will also be possible to attend the scheduled appointments, together with visiting the exhibitions and the moments dedicated to books, documentation and performance.
For the museum, the initiative offers the opportunity to get closer to some of the artistic research present in the exhibitions and to deepen the relationship between contemporary art, documentation, publishing and performative practices. The finissage thus brings together the three exhibitions and the activities organised for the XXII Contemporary Day. ### Books, documentation and research
The publishing component revolves around the series «i Quaderni – Italia 2050 Research Center of the MA*GA Museum», published by Nomos Edizioni. At the heart of the event are two volumes linked to the exhibitions coming to a close and to the themes addressed by the museum during the day.
The first is «The roads end before they begin. Vincenzo Agnetti and photographic traces». The presentation involves Alessandro Castiglioni, Germana Agnetti and Achille Filipponi. The volume takes up the title of the exhibition dedicated to Vincenzo Agnetti and photographic traces, bringing one of the paths proposed by the museum into the publishing program.
The second volume is «Here and elsewhere. Paolo Scheggi’s environments 1964–1971», presented with Emma Zanella, Ilaria Bignotti and Cosima Scheggi. In this case too, the title of the book corresponds to that of the exhibition dedicated to Paolo Scheggi’s environments. The two publishing events are therefore directly linked to the exhibitions that conclude their run at the MA*GA.
The day places video, performance and the catalogue dedicated to «ARTE VIVA. Performative and participatory processes as practice. XXVIII Gallarate Prize» alongside the books. The relationship between contemporary art and documentation thus moves from the research displayed in the galleries to the publications presented during the initiative.
The museum describes the event as an opportunity to learn more about the artistic research explored by the exhibitions. The presence of the series, the two volumes and the catalogue broadens the closing event beyond the visit alone, keeping publishing, research and performative practices at the center, the areas identified for the XXII AMACI Contemporary Day. ### The events, hour by hour
The sequence of events will begin at 16 with the screening of the video «Vincenzo Agnetti, Elisabetta d’Inghilterra. Lecture-performance 37a Biennale di Venezia, 1976». The first part of the program will therefore be devoted to video content related to research on Vincenzo Agnetti.
At 16.20, institutional greetings are scheduled. Ten minutes later, at 16.30, the series «i Quaderni – Italia 2050 Centro di ricerca del Museo MA*GA», published by Nomos Edizioni, will be presented. This part of the schedule includes the two volumes devoted to the exhibitions «Le strade terminano prima di cominciare. Vincenzo Agnetti e le tracce fotografiche» and «Qui e altrove. Gli ambienti di Paolo Scheggi 1964–1971».
At 17.15, Michele Lombardelli’s performance «NEG», created in collaboration with the Archivio Vincenzo Agnetti, will be presented. At 17.45, the program will return to publishing with the presentation of the catalogue «ARTE VIVA. Processi performativi e partecipativi come pratica. XXVIII Premio Gallarate», together with Alessandro Castiglioni and Emma Zanella.
Closing the program at 18 will be Martina Rota’s «Until there’s no air», included in the MILANoLTRE festival. The schedule guides the audience from the opening video to the publishing presentation, from the performance to the closing event entrusted to Martina Rota.
Throughout the day, it will be possible to visit the Museo MA*GA free of charge and attend the scheduled events. The schedule for 10 ottobre thus combines a visit to the three exhibitions, the finissage and the meetings devoted to books, video, research and performance.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/al-museo-maga-di-gallarate-la-xxii-giornata-del-contemporaneo-tra-libri-performance-e-ricerca/2696764/)*

item.title: Festival of Cairate 2026: art, flavours and music at the Monastery
item.description: On Sunday 4 October 2026 from 10, the sixteenth Cairate Festival takes place at the Monastero di Santa Maria Assunta with Camminar Gustando (10 € card) and a concert on Saturday 3 October at 21.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Cairate Festival: sixteenth edition on October 4, 2026 - Santa Maria Assunta Monastery at the center of the day - Exhibitions, visits, games, sports and Camminar Gustando - Linee d'Archi concert on Saturday, October 3 at 9 p.m.
## Key facts - What → Cairate Festival - When → Sunday, October 4, 2026, from 10 a.m. - Where → Santa Maria Assunta Monastery and adjacent streets - Organization → Pro Loco, with the patronage of the Municipality - Camminar Gustando → from 12 p.m. to 2:30 p.m., ticket 10 euros - Concert → Saturday, October 3 at 9 p.m., Cairate Auditorium
On Sunday, October 4, 2026, starting at 10 a.m., Cairate will host the sixteenth edition of the Cairate Festival. The event is organized by Pro Loco with the patronage of the Municipality and will have as its heart the Santa Maria Assunta Monastery, together with the exhibition spaces and the surrounding streets and squares.
It is a village festival immersed in over a thousand years of history. The day will combine art, culture, gastronomy and entertainment, with initiatives distributed inside the monastic complex and in the nearby areas. The public will be welcomed in one of the most fascinating historic sites in the Province of Varese, a complex whose origins date back to the Lombard age and which still today preserves the traces of the various phases of its long history.
### The Santa Maria Assunta Monastery
The monastery represents the reference point of the event also for the historical value of the place. Tradition traces its foundation back to 737 AD, at the wish of the Lombard noblewoman Manigunda. Historical studies, however, place the origins of the complex between the Lombard period and the Early Middle Ages.
For centuries the monastery was an economic and social reference point for Cairate. Its architecture preserves a stratification that tells more than a millennium of history, while the great cloister organizes the spaces of the complex. It is in this setting that the activities of the Cairate Festival will unfold, among halls, exhibition areas, streets and squares.
The sixteenth edition thus retains the popular character of a village festival and pairs it with the opportunity to enter a historic place, get to know its surroundings and experience its spaces during a day open to the public. The programme includes exhibitions, guided tours, family‑oriented proposals, sports activities, entertainment and a gastronomic route set up in the monastery garden. ## Exhibitions, visits and activities in the complex
The spaces of the Monastery of Santa Maria Assunta will host several exhibitions with different opening dates. The exhibition "Acquerelli dell'Anima" by Patrizia Gosio will be visitable from September 26 to October 4. Until October 11, instead, "Scopofobia – When the fear of being observed dominates thought" and "Ugo Zovetti – Homo" will remain on display.
On the sole day of Sunday, October 4, there will also be an artistic exhibition curated by L'Arca Cooperativa Sociale. The exhibitions will therefore accompany the feast within the monastic complex, alongside the other initiatives, offering a dedicated art proposal.
### Guided visits and the market
Another appointment will be represented by guided tours of the Monastery, conducted by the volunteers of Pro Loco. The complex is developed around the large cloister and preserves testimonies of the different phases of its history, besides archaeological traces of the Lombard era.
Local tradition also wants that Frederick Barbarossa was hosted in the guesthouse on the eve of the Battle of Legnano. This story adds to the historical and archaeological elements that will be part of the visit to the monastery during the day.
Outside the complex, there will be space for the market of hobbyists and non-profit associations of the territory. The proposal will widen the festival area beyond the monastic environments, involving the streets and squares surrounding the historic site.
### Games, sports and flavors
Ample space will be reserved for families. The Lombarda Pompieri Sempre ODV Association will curate recreational activities and inflatables, while the Hornets Tradate will propose softball and baseball demonstrations dedicated to boys.
The program will also include a table football tournament curated by the Pro Loco of Lonate Ceppino, the Kamishibai theatre, giant chess and other entertainment proposals.
Finally, in the monastery garden, Il Camminar Gustando will return, an active gastronomic path from 12 to 14:30. The cards, available until sold out, will cost 10 euros and will allow discovering the gastronomic proposals while walking in one of the most suggestive corners of the town. ## The appointment calendar
The Festival of Cairate will begin on Saturday, October 3, before the main day scheduled for Sunday. At 9 pm, at the Auditorium of Cairate, the concert of the group Linee d 'Archi is scheduled. The title of the evening will be Soli e tutti, instrumental music between the 18th and 19th centuries, a musical path dedicated to the 18th and 19th centuries. Entrance will be free.
The second appointment is scheduled for Sunday, October 4, with the start of the initiatives at 10 am. The main day will take place between the Monastery of Cairate and the adjacent streets, gathering in a single program the activities planned in the historic complex and in the surrounding spaces.
### Two days, two party venues
The calendar can be read following the sequence indicated by the organizers:
| Date | Appointment | Time and place | |---|---|---| | Saturday 3 October | Concert of Lines of Arches | 21 Hours, Auditorium of Cairate | | Sunday, October 4 | Main Day of the Festival of Cairate | From 10 am, Monastery and adjacent streets |
The concert of the Auditorium will therefore anticipate the Sunday program of the monastery. The first evening will be dedicated to instrumental music, while the next day will bring together exhibitions, visits, recreational activities, sports, entertainment and gastronomy in the spaces of the event.
Sunday will not be concentrated in a single environment: the initiatives will be spread among the monastic complex and the surrounding streets and squares.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/la-festa-di-cairate-torna-tra-arte-sapori-e-spettacoli-nello-splendido-monastero/2695852/)*

item.title: Varese approves 10,8 million loan for the new theater
item.description: The City Council approved the budget adjustment that brings the investment to approximately 22 million, with a loan from Cassa Depositi e Prestiti of 10,8 million.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The City Council approves the budget adjustment - Total investment rises to approximately 22 million euros - The loan from Cassa Depositi e Prestiti reaches 10,8 million - The vote ends with 19 in favor and 8 against
- Date → giovedì 1 ottobre - Place → Villa Recalcati - Investment → approximately 22 million euros - Expenditure adjustment → approximately 3,35 million euros - Loan → 10,8 million euros - Entity → Cassa Depositi e Prestiti - Votes → 19 in favor and 8 against - GSE contribution temporarily replaced → 1,195 million euros
The Varese City Council approved the budget adjustment for the new theater that is expected to be built on the site of the former Politeama. The decision came on giovedì 1 ottobre, at the session held at Villa Recalcati: 19 councilors voted in favor and 8 against. The result confirmed the division between the majority and minority.
With the adjustment, total investment is brought to approximately 22 million euros. The figures were presented by Budget Councillor Ivana Buzzetti, who gave two reasons for the update. The first concerns the temporary replacement of the GSE contribution intended for energy efficiency improvements. The ranking, she explained, does not currently appear to have been reopened, although the application submitted remains valid. The second reason is the request to adjust the prices and the project's overall design.
### The adjustment and funding sources
The accounting result of the change is an expenditure adjustment quantified at approximately 3,35 million euros. Of this amount, 1,195 million is linked to the temporary loss of the GSE contribution. The previous framework provided for 500 thousand euros in provincial contribution, 1,5 million in municipal surplus, 6,27 million in loan financing, 9,4 million in regional contribution and 1,19 million in GSE contribution.
With the new arrangement, the funding sources were redefined. The Province's 500 thousand euros remain, while the Municipality contributes 1,5 million from unrestricted surplus. The Region contributes 9,4 million and the loan is increased to 10,8 million euros. The new framework temporarily replaces the GSE share with a larger loan component, without changing the other amounts reported in the adjustment. ## The debate in the council
The opposition voted against it, bringing back into the council debate the arguments already presented in committee. Lega councillors Monti and Angei focused above all on the location of the project. In their view, it would have been preferable to expand or make the theatre in Piazza Repubblica permanent, rather than build the new structure on the site of the former Politeama.
The disagreement also concerns the nature of the site. Fondazione Molina granted the Municipality surface rights for 90 years, but ownership of the property belongs to an entity other than the municipal authority. For Lega councillors, this characteristic weighs in the assessment of the project. Their objections also included the costs which, in their view, would fall on the residents of Varese and future municipal administrations.
Guido Bonoldi, a representative of Lavoriamo per Varese, took part in the debate. His reference to the origins of the agreement goes back to spring 2021, when he was president of Fondazione Molina and signed the agreement between the Foundation and the Municipality. The Foundation, which owns the former Politeama property, had granted the Municipality surface rights for 90 years to allow the construction of the new theatre as part of the programme agreement.
This brought the relationship between the construction project and the private site back into the council discussion, one of the points contested by the minority. Bonoldi reconstructed the role of the agreement signed in 2021 and the possibility of using the former Politeama property for the municipal project.
Councillor for Culture Enzo Laforgia referred to the points already highlighted in the interview given to VareseNews. His position was summed up in the idea that the new theatre should not be considered the theatre of a single administration, but that of the entire city of Varese. Thus, the debate kept the criticisms concerning the site, ownership and costs distinct from the vision of the project as a city-wide initiative. ## What happens now
### The loan linked to progress on the works
The approved change also defines how the new financing is to be used. The 10,8-million loan is structured as a flexible loan with a pre-amortization period from Cassa Depositi e Prestiti. It can be disbursed according to the progress of the works, in relation to the progress of the project indicated in the spending schedule. To optimize financial costs, the entity chose to split the amount into 7,57 million for 2027 and 3,23 million for 2028.
### The spending review clause
The resolution also includes a clause linked to the national legislation on spending review, referred to as Article 1, paragraph 8, of Law 207/2024. The clause provides for the setting aside of resources for 2026 and 2027. Once established in the financial statement, those sums will have to be allocated to the gradual reduction of the portion of the loan originally authorized for the theater. The mechanism set out in the measure therefore links the use of the resources to their ascertainment in the financial statement and the subsequent reduction of the authorized portion of the loan.
The source also specifies that the replacement of the GSE contribution is temporary and that the application submitted remains valid, even though the ranking for energy efficiency does not currently appear to have been reopened.
### The spaces envisaged by the project
Regarding the works, it emerged in committee that the current structure of the former Politeama will be demolished before construction of the new theater. The project also provides for the use of other adjacent spaces, including the former offices of the social services department. Bonoldi linked the closure of the Tezenis store, which previously occupied the building, to this need: according to his recollection, Fondazione Molina did not renew the contract specifically to free up the space needed for the project.
The framework outlined after the vote therefore includes the loan’s annual allocations, the disbursement linked to progress on the works and the reduction clause, together with the demolition of the existing structure and the use of the nearby areas envisaged by the project.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/nuovo-teatro-di-varese-approvato-il-mutuo-da-108-milioni-con-cassa-depositi/2695819/)*

item.title: Varesina-Pro Patria derby: Sunday's clash
item.description: Sunday 4 October at 15 at Elmec Solar Stadium: Pro Patria (12 points) are looking for a reaction, Varesina (4) for a turning point.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Varesina-Pro Patria derby on Sunday 4 October at 15 - It will be played at the Elmec Solar Stadium in Venegono Superiore - Pro Patria have taken 12 points from four wins - Varesina have lost their last three matches
## Key facts - Match: Varesina-Pro Patria - Venue: Elmec Solar Stadium, Venegono Superiore - Time: Sunday 4 October, 15 - Varesina's latest result: 4-2 defeat to Casatese Merate - Standings: Pro Patria 12 points, Varesina 4
On Sunday 4 October at 15, at the Elmec Solar Stadium in Venegono Superiore, Varesina and Pro Patria will face each other in a derby presented as a match worth more than three points. The blue-and-whites come into it after their first league defeat, while the Phoenixes are looking for a response capable of ending their negative run.
The two sides come into the match with different needs. Pro Patria have collected 12 points from four consecutive wins, before coming to a halt at home against Solbiatese. The setback changed the tone of the build-up, but not the stated objective: the Little Tigers must react immediately to avoid losing ground to the teams at the top. In the standings, Pistoiese are first with 15 points; Pro Sesto and Pro Patria follow on 12.
### Pro Patria's build-up
At the pre-match press conference, coach Zironelli asked the team to regain clarity and decisiveness. The coach distinguished technical errors, considered part of football, from tactical ones, which in his view must not be repeated. The defeat against Solbiatese was framed as part of a broader process, with a call to put the setback behind them immediately:
> «Now we reset and start again.»
Zironelli also confirmed the decision to play attacking football, with more players involved in ball management and attacking play. He explained that the team does not intend to be influenced by comparisons with their opponents and that, ahead of the derby and another run of closely spaced matches, rotations are possible to involve every member of the squad.
### Varesina's comeback bid
Varesina began with a win against Cittadella Modena, but in the following matchdays alternated good performances with difficulties, before suffering three consecutive defeats. The latest, away to Casatese Merate, ended 4-2. The Phoenixes need consistency and confidence, especially since they sit on 4 points in the standings, level with Tropical Coriano. item.title: Brawl in Saronno: two young people injured during the night
item.description: Two men aged 25 and 27 were injured in a brawl in the pedestrian center of Saronno: three ambulances and carabinieri at the scene.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Brawl among young people in Saronno's historic centre - Two young men aged 25 and 27 injured - Three ambulances in the pedestrian area - Investigations by the carabinieri of the Saronno Company
## Key facts - Date → night between Friday 2 and Saturday 3 October - Time → shortly before 0.30 - Location → between Piazza Libertà and Via Garibaldi - Injured → two young men aged 25 and 27 - Emergency response → three ambulances - Outcome → hospital, yellow code and green code - Forces involved → carabinieri of the Saronno Company
Shortly before 0.30, on the night between Friday 2 and Saturday 3 October, an argument between some young people turned into a brawl in the historic centre of Saronno. The alarm was raised in the heart of the pedestrian area, between Piazza Libertà and Via Garibaldi, after the group's shouting drew attention.
The confrontation was taking place noisily when the situation quickly worsened. The reconstruction reports that a group of young people, apparently foreigners, were engaged in an argument. When emergency services reached the area, however, the other participants had already left. Two young men, identified as the people in need of assistance, remained on the ground.
They are two young men aged 25 and 27. Both were taken to hospital after the ambulances arrived; they were assigned a yellow code and a green code. Their condition is described as battered, but the two were not in danger. The reported medical picture therefore remains that of injured people taken to hospital, with no indication of danger.
The sequence recounted begins with the shouting and ends, immediately afterwards, with the two young men being taken to hospital. Between these two moments, the argument quickly escalated from a noisy confrontation into a brawl, while the other people involved left the area. It is this sequence of events, which took place in the pedestrian heart of the city, that the reconstruction of what happened focuses on. ### The emergency response
The emergency response activated after the alarm involved three ambulances. Croce rossa di Saronno, Sos Uboldo and Croce azzurra di Rovellasca arrived at the scene. The source therefore indicates three organizations involved in assisting the two young men, who were then transferred to hospital with yellow and green codes.
The medical outcome reported in the reconstruction concerns two young people, aged 25 and 27, in poor condition but not in danger. Hospitalization is indicated for both, while the codes reported are one yellow and one green. These are the data available on the immediate outcome of the medical intervention.
| Element | Detail | |---|---| | Ambulances | Three | | Organizations | Croce rossa di Saronno; Sos Uboldo; Croce azzurra di Rovellasca | | Outcome | Two young people in hospital, yellow and green codes |
The intervention by the law enforcement forces accompanied the medical intervention. Several patrols of the carabinieri of the Compagnia di Saronno reached the historic center. The source places the presence of the officers in the same scene in which the screams had signaled the fight and in which, when the emergency responders arrived, the other participants had already left.
The final reference concerns public order during nighttime hours in the city center. The episode in fact draws attention to an issue already mentioned in the description of the city: in the past, the historic center had been the scene of fights and moments of tension. The reference to previous incidents remains part of the local context provided by the source. The outcome of the night is that the two young men were taken to hospital. ### The investigations
The follow-up to the incident is now in the hands of the Carabinieri of the Saronno Company, who are trying to reconstruct precisely what happened. Their activity has three objectives indicated by the source: clarifying the dynamics of the altercation, understanding the reasons that caused it to escalate, and identifying the other people who allegedly took part in it.
The work starts from a situation already defined in its essential features: the shouts of a group in the pedestrian area, the transformation of the argument into a brawl, two young people injured and the other participants already gone by the time emergency services arrived. The reasons for the altercation are another point to clarify. The available account does not indicate an already established motive and reports that the officers are working precisely to clarify why the discussion escalated. As for the identifications, attention is focused on the other people who allegedly took part in the incident before leaving.
This phase therefore concerns both the dynamics and the participants. The intervention of several Carabinieri patrols opened the investigations in the historic center, while the source identifies as its objective a precise reconstruction of what happened. The documented local follow-up remains investigative: clarifying the reasons for the altercation and identifying those who allegedly took part in it are the steps entrusted to the officers.

item.description: Carabinieri of Luino carry out a pre-trial detention order in prison by order of the GIP of Varese. A crossbow was found at home.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Carabinieri of Luino carry out a pre-trial detention order in prison - The man is 46 years old and was already under house arrest - The complaint was filed by his partner - A crossbow complete with bolts was seized at the home
## Key facts - Location → Luino - When → afternoon of lunedì 28 settembre - Age → 46 years old - Authority → GIP of the Court of Varese - Measure → pre-trial detention in prison - Reported charges → sexual violence and domestic abuse - Victim → partner - Seizure → rifle crossbow complete with bolts
### The precautionary measure
On the afternoon of lunedì 28 settembre, the Carabinieri of the Luino Station carried out an order for pre-trial detention in prison against a 46-year-old man residing in the area. The order had been issued by the GIP of the Court of Varese.
The man was already under house arrest. The measure was triggered following the complaint filed by his partner, who told investigators what allegedly happened during the period they lived together. In the proceedings, the 46-year-old is considered responsible for sexual violence and domestic abuse against the woman.
The complaint led to the investigations that preceded the new measure. During the investigation, investigators reconstructed the facts reported by his partner and linked the proceedings to the conduct attributed to the man within the family.
The circumstances concern the period they lived together, during which the woman allegedly suffered ongoing abuse, physical assaults, and degrading conduct. The episodes were described by investigators in the investigative work that led to the pre-trial detention.
The transition from house arrest to prison is the central fact of the operation carried out in Luino. The man, already under house arrest, was served with the order issued by the GIP of the Court of Varese.
The Carabinieri of the Luino Station carried out the order on the afternoon of lunedì 28 settembre. The case remains linked to the complaint filed by the partner and the reconstruction carried out during the investigations. In the proceedings, the 46-year-old is considered responsible for the conduct described as having been directed against the woman. ## The Reconstructed Incidents
### Threats, Assaults and Sexual Violence
According to the reconstruction made during the investigation, his partner allegedly suffered continuous abuse, physical assaults and demeaning behavior for several years during their cohabitation. The picture described by investigators therefore includes behavior repeated over time, relating to the couple's family life.
On several occasions, the man allegedly threatened the woman by holding a knife to her throat and directing serious insults at her. Some of these situations allegedly also occurred in the presence of the couple's two minor children. The presence of the children is indicated in the reconstruction of the incidents relating to their cohabitation.
The most serious incidents concern the last two years. On two separate occasions, the 46-year-old allegedly forced his partner to endure non-consensual sexual intercourse. The allegation concerns events occurring in the most recent phase of the cohabitation period, while the other abuse is described as having continued for several years.
The escalation of violence allegedly recently also involved the victim's sister, the man's sister-in-law. The argument, which arose over trivial reasons, allegedly degenerated into an assault: the woman was struck in the face and pushed against a wall. She subsequently suffered injuries deemed curable in ten days.
The reconstruction thus brings together incidents against the partner and an assault involving one of her family members. For the cohabiting woman, the proceedings began with her complaint; for the sister, investigators identified a recent incident involving injuries deemed curable in ten days. These are the elements described in the investigative framework. ## The follow-up to the operation
### The search and seizure
During the operation to execute the precautionary measure, Carabinieri personnel carried out a search inside the man's home. During the checks, the Carabinieri found a rifle crossbow complete with bolts inside a wardrobe. The crossbow was immediately seized.
The discovery took place during the search conducted as part of the operation. The crossbow was found inside a wardrobe in the home and, together with the bolts, was immediately seized. The seizure was carried out by Carabinieri personnel during the operations.
At the end of the activities, the 46-year-old man was taken to Miogni prison in Varese, at the disposal of the judicial authorities. The investigation was coordinated by the Varese Public Prosecutor's Office.
The immediate follow-up to the operation therefore includes the seizure of the object found in the home and the man's transfer to Miogni. His destination in Varese and his being placed at the disposal of the judicial authorities are indicated at the end of the personnel's activities.
As a side note to the operation, the Arma dei Carabinieri renewed its invitation to all victims of violence, abuse or oppression to promptly report the facts. The appeal concerns the possibility of confidently contacting the Single Emergency Number 112 or directly contacting the Carabinieri Stations spread throughout the area.
The personnel emphasized that every report may prove fundamental in putting an end to dangerous situations. The invitation accompanies the account of the operation and reiterates that the prompt reporting of facts can help put an end to dangerous situations.

item.title: Varese: 70 kg of drugs in camper, arrests
item.description: The Guardia di Finanza stops a Spanish camper van: 19 kg of cocaine, 49 of marijuana seized, and a dachshund entrusted to a family.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - More than 70 kilos of drugs seized - Two Spaniards and one Italian arrested - The shipment would have yielded more than 5 million euros - Operation in the wooded areas of the province of Varese
## Key facts - What → more than 70 kilos of drugs - Where → wooded areas of the province of Varese - Who → two 55-year-old Spaniards and a 34-year-old Italian - Money → 6.600 euros - Proceeds from drug dealing → more than five million euros
### Observation of the convoy More than 70 kilos of drugs were seized in the wooded areas of the province of Varese, where the Guardia di Finanza arrested three people. The operation was carried out by the Varese Provincial Command of the Guardia di Finanza as part of economic checks in the area.
Those stopped were a couple of 55-year-old Spanish citizens and a 34-year-old Italian man, resident in the province of Varese. The two Spaniards were traveling in a camper van with a Spanish license plate, while the Fiat 500 following the vehicle was driven by the Italian. Watson, a small fawn Brittany dachshund, was also in the camper.
During one of their routine patrols, the Guardia di Finanza officers of the Varese Economic and Financial Police Unit noticed the camper van moving slowly toward the wooded areas of the province, turning onto a dead-end dirt road. These are areas known for drug dealing. At close distance behind the vehicle, the Fiat 500 was traveling.
The route of the two vehicles, which were proceeding in convoy, aroused the officers' suspicions. The patrol maintained its distance and requested the intervention of another support unit. In the meantime, the officers hid among the dense vegetation to verify the occupants' intentions.
The convoy reached a clearing at the foot of the woods. After looking around, the occupants of the camper van unloaded a first large duffel bag and placed it in the trunk of the Fiat 500. The car was driven by the Italian, the intended recipient of the drugs.
Believing that a transfer of drugs was taking place and after reinforcements arrived, the officers intervened. The people present were detained, and numerous cocaine bricks were found in the duffel bag just loaded into the small car, bearing the distinctive effigy of the hero Superman. The operation led to the arrest of the three individuals, and the investigation was extended to the camper van and the Italian's home. ### The substances and objects found The seizure included an assortment of different substances. The recovered material included 19 kilograms of cocaine, 49 kilograms of marijuana and 1,9 kilograms of hashish. These quantities were joined by 72 grams of heroin, 233 LSD blotters and 200 ecstasy pills. All the material was seized by the Guardia di Finanza.
Part of the cocaine had a particular composition. The substance had been mixed with methamphetamines and artificially flavored, according to what was reported during the operation, with strawberry, grape, coconut and melon flavors. The stated objective was so-called criminal marketing, with a characterization of the product intended for drug dealing.
During the searches, 6.600 euros in cash were also recovered, a sum identified as proceeds from drug dealing. Investigators also found two precision scales. The seizure also included a taser, a machete, a baseball bat, a telescopic baton and a folding knife.
The search of the camper and of the home of the Italian man who was to receive the drugs made it possible to complete the recovery of the material. The Comando Provinciale della Guardia di Finanza di Varese thus seized both the substances and the objects found during the checks, simultaneously arresting the three people present.
According to the reconstruction provided by the Fiamme Gialle, selling the entire load would have yielded more than five million euros. The figure concerns the value that the sale of the seized material could have generated, consisting of cocaine, marijuana, hashish, heroin, LSD and ecstasy.
The operation is part of the economic control of the territory carried out by the Comando Provinciale, including in areas near the wooded areas of the province. The stated aim is to prevent and combat the possession of narcotic substances intended for drug dealing. The operation therefore concerned both the transfer of the bag and the contents kept in the camper and in the home that was searched. ### Referral to the Judicial Authority After the arrest, the three individuals were taken to the prisons in Varese and Como. They were placed at the disposal of the Judicial Authority of Varese, which has jurisdiction over the proceedings connected to the Guardia di Finanza operation.
The Judicial Authority of Varese validated the searches, the seizure and the arrest. The arrested individuals must answer charges of drug trafficking and possession of improvised weapons. The source does not indicate any further judicial developments beyond the measures already validated.
A separate follow-up concerned Watson, the small dachshund present in the camper. The dog proved extremely patient and docile throughout all stages of the operation. After the vehicle was stopped, he was initially cared for at the barracks by Guardia di Finanza officers.
Subsequently, Watson was entrusted to a family that voluntarily offered to provide temporary adoption. The accommodation was therefore found after the assistance he received at the barracks, while the three arrested individuals were being transferred to the prisons in Varese and Como.
The operation is also presented by the Fiamme Gialle as a testament to the Guardia di Finanza's strong social vocation. Alongside its typical economic and financial police function, the Corps works to protect the entire community, intervening against phenomena considered to pose a particular social alarm and a danger to public safety and health.
These phenomena include the trafficking and dealing of narcotic substances, which were at the center of the intervention in the wooded areas of the province of Varese. The seizure of the consignment, the validation of the measures and Watson's temporary placement represent the developments indicated by the source after the camper and the Fiat 500 were stopped.

item.title: Carluccio Nursery School Como: staff writes to the Municipality
item.description: The staff of the Carluccio preschool on Via Volta writes to the Mayor to oppose the cuts: the school is not a cost, but a community investment.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - After September 28, the staff wrote a new letter. - Carluccio is the preschool on via Volta in Como. - The positive ruling: Carluccio remains open. - Signed by Bozzi, ten teachers and the school assistant.
## Key facts - Location → Carluccio preschool, via Volta, Como - Document → letter from Maria Grazia Bozzi - Signatories → ten teachers and the school assistant - Debate → reorganization involving closures and mergers - Precedent → closure decided by the Municipal Administration two years ago - Appeal → TAR, filed to defend the school - Outcome → positive ruling: Carluccio remains open - Symbol → olive tree given by Comitato Nova Como in September
After the City Council meeting of September 28, Carluccio preschool is once again at the center of the debate over the reorganization of schools in Como. The reorganization sought by the Rapinese administration provides for closures and mergers; the majority approved a resolution on the downsizing of schools. It is from this development that the new letter from the staff of the preschool on via Volta stems.
The letter is signed by Maria Grazia Bozzi, the school’s representative. The document also bears the signatures of ten teachers and the school assistant. The letter is addressed to the Mayor and the Councillor for Education and Educational Policies and argues that one cannot remain indifferent in the face of the resolution. The text makes clear that it does not intend to repeat the explanations already set out in previous letters concerning the effects of mergers and closures; instead, it chooses to return to the reality of Carluccio.
The text recalls what happened two years ago. The Municipal Administration had decided on the closure of the school. Families, committees, teachers and the entire school community did not remain indifferent to that decision. Thanks to the determination of the families, the committees and, in particular, Comitato Nova Como, together with the teachers and Istituto Comprensivo Como Borgovico, a campaign was launched to defend Carluccio. The process also led to an appeal to the TAR. Then came the positive ruling: the school remained open.
Teachers, parents and the entire Istituto Comprensivo Como Borgovico celebrated that decision, because Carluccio is not simply a place in which to welcome children. For the staff, it is a school founded on educational values, on a specific view of the child and on a pedagogical project built day after day. The letter thus calls into question an understanding of the school based solely on organizational or numerical criteria, as if it were merely the place where children are left while their parents work. The position expressed is unequivocal: Carluccio must be considered for what it represents educationally and within the community, not merely for its place in the reorganization of schools. ### An Educational Project Built Every Day
La Carluccio is described as a socio-educational hub in the heart of the city of Como. In the document, attention shifts from the organizational aspect to the meaning of preschool. It is the first educational environment in which children experience relationships with others, learn to share and communicate, recognize their own emotions and those of others, and gradually become independent. For the letter, these steps describe the school’s daily work.
The structure of the project moves from sections to spaces, from workshops to the schedule of the day and the stable presence of teachers. The document considers them integral parts of the educational project, not secondary components to be improvised. The environments must be designed to allow children to explore, experiment, play, create, and learn. The stable presence of teachers also has an educational and relational function: the reference figures know each child’s development, characteristics, vulnerabilities, and potential.
The word continuity occupies a central place in the letter. Continuity means not viewing each school year as an isolated experience, but building a path that accompanies the child as they grow. The educational thread must connect teachers, families, and the local community and, subsequently, preschool and primary school. Time and conditions are also needed to observe each child in their uniqueness: not everyone learns in the same way, not everyone has the same pace, and not everyone expresses their needs through words.
La Carluccio is also described as a place of inclusion. Differences can become a source of enrichment, and every child must be able to find their own space, feel part of the group, and develop their potential. This reading leads to criticism of an assessment based solely on the number of enrolled children, the spaces occupied, or a financial statement. A school is made up of relationships, skills, experiences, professionalism, and community. La Carluccio, the staff writes, represents all of this.
Another element mentioned in the letter is the olive tree donated to the school by Comitato Nova Como last school year, in September. The tree was chosen as a symbol of rebirth, strength, and resilience. For teachers and school staff, it aptly represents the school: once again, they have started anew with determination and passion, continuing to believe in the value of their work and in the strength of the educational project. ### The request to listen to the community
The letter indicates the criterion to follow before making decisions about Carluccio's future. The staff asks that those who experience the school every day be listened to: the children, families, teachers and all the school staff. The document specifies that the value of the school concerns not only the families who attend it today, but the entire community. For this reason, the assessment of its future should not stop at the premises, the numbers or the economic dimension mentioned in the text.
The point called for by the authors therefore concerns recognizing the network built over time. According to the letter, closing or scaling back a preschool would mean breaking up a network of relationships and weakening an educational hub. That network includes the relationship between children, families, teachers and the local area, along with the path connecting preschool to primary school. Carluccio is thus presented as an institution that belongs to the community, not merely to the families who attend it today.
The document then returns to the image of roots. Carluccio school has already shown that it has deep roots, and the olive tree donated by Comitato Nova Como has become their symbol. Those roots, the staff writes, ask to be respected, nurtured and allowed to grow. Behind a school there are not only walls and numbers: there are children, people, relationships, an educational project and a community. The letter links to this heritage the idea that a community capable of investing in its children also invests in its future.
The signatures make the position expressed in the document a collective one. In addition to the representative Maria Grazia Bozzi, the teachers Angelica Sansone, Giorgia Marchio, Paola Della Bosca, Sabrina Ghielmetti, Domenica Previtali, Virginia Fiandaca, Manuela Ghislanzoni, Lucia D'Angelo, Francesca Pellegrino and Silvana Somaini sign. The school support staff member identified is Nunzia Battista.
> «The school is not a cost to be reduced: it is an investment to be protected.»
This is the phrase with which the staff summarizes the request for protection addressed to those who will have to deal with the future of the Carluccio preschool.
*Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/attualita/como-lettera-da-tutto-il-personale-dellasilo-carluccio-la-scuola-non-e-un-costo-da-ridurre-qui-ce-una-comunita/)*

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Varese host Pergine on Saturday at 18.30 - Mastini and Linci are on 3 points - Vanetti and Terzago remain out - Franchini may be called up
## Key facts - Game → Varese-Pergine - Venue → Acinque Ice Arena - Standings → Varese, Pergine and Feltre are on 3 points - Absences → Vanetti and Terzago - Shots on goal → Varese 35, Caldaro 33 - Power play → figure reversed compared with last year
At 18.30 on Saturday, Varese's Mastini host Pergine at the Acinque Ice Arena. It is a direct clash between two mid-table teams: Varese, Pergine and Feltre are level on 3 points, six points behind the Caldaro-Aosta duo. The game is part of the fourth matchday of the IHL and comes after the Mastini's away game at Caldaro.
The game in South Tyrol left one certainty and one obligation. The certainty concerns the character of the team coached by Dave Rich. Trailing 3-0 after less than nine minutes, the black-and-yellow side got back into the game in the second period. Then Selva's goal, scored 11 seconds before the second buzzer, shifted the momentum toward the Lucci, who managed to confirm their superiority in the third period.
The obligation is to turn that reaction into points against a Pergine side described as a strong team. The Linci will also bring their supporters to the Acinque Ice Arena, while Varese will have to reproduce the quick attacks and offensive play shown in the last outing.
### A team with more options
Against Caldaro, the Mastini finished with 35 shots on goal, compared with 33 attempts by their opponents. The numbers reflect an attack with several options: Bastille, De Toni, Borghi, Piroso and the new arrival Glasman are listed among the most dangerous players up front.
The defense also offered positive signs, although it needs reinforcements to preserve energy and focus. Filippo Matonti was once again among the best. Among the goaltenders, Leonardo Mordenti's return home is also noted. Another positive element is the power play, described as completely transformed compared with last year.
### The roster and the home-ice factor
Dave Rich will decide whether to dress Franchini based on the forward's physical condition. Captain Vanetti will remain out for around twenty days because of a muscle problem, while Terzago is still unavailable. The absence of both forces the defense to operate with a five-man rotation.
The performances against Fassa and Caldaro are presented as an incentive to fill the arena. According to the game preview, the black-and-yellow faithful will have to be the extra man on the ice. The comparison between Varese and Pergine’s campaigns explains why the game has the profile of a direct clash, without turning the standings into a prediction. After three matchdays, both teams have 3 points, along with Feltre, while Caldaro and Aosta lead with 9.
| Team | Campaign in the opening matchdays | |---|---| | Varese | Home defeat to Appiano 2-4; win at Fassa 5-3; away game at Caldaro | | Pergine | Home defeat to Fassa 3-6; comeback against Val Pusteria Junior 4-3; home defeat to Appiano 1-5 |
The most useful reference point is Fassa. Varese won on its ice, while Pergine lost at home against the same team. It is the comparison that warrants a fair degree of optimism, but the same source reminds us that every game is a story unto itself. The outcome of the direct clash will therefore depend on the ability to reproduce the positive indications on the ice, not merely on the sequence of previous games.
### The Linci profile
Pergine should not be underestimated either because of last season’s campaign. The Linci of Valsugana finished fifth and, in the playoff quarterfinals, immediately overturned home-ice advantage against Appiano. This is a precedent that supports a cautious reading of the game.
James Thomas Dowd is the name identified as the main offensive reference point. He has already scored against Fassa and Appiano and has been well supported by Foccoli, Bitetto and Dellmar Speranza. Andreotti, meanwhile, is described as a player capable of striking in crucial moments. Defensively, some uncertainty remains in the Linci’s setup: this is the weak point the Mastini will have to try to exploit.
### The key to the clash
The game therefore pits Varese’s offensive variety against an opponent that has shown quality, but also possible vulnerability at the back. The Pergine crowd will be passionate, while the yellow-and-black crowd is called upon to support the team at the Acinque Ice Arena. 1. Check Varese's lineup. The decision regarding Franchini will depend on the forward's physical condition. Vanetti and Terzago remain out, forcing the defense to rotate with five men.
2. Watch the start. In Caldaro, the Mastini were down 3-0 after less than nine minutes, but they reacted in the second period. Managing the start will therefore be one of the first elements to observe.
3. Measure offensive production. Against Caldaro, Varese shot 35 times, while their opponents finished 33 times. Fast transitions and the ability to involve Bastille, De Toni, Borghi, Piroso, and Glasman represent the benchmarks indicated on the eve of the match.

item.title: Hockey, Ambrì conquer the BCF Arena: Fribourg beaten 2-1
item.description: After two defeats, Ambrì rediscover their solidity and win 2-1 in Fribourg. Goals by Müller and Schnarr prove decisive in an evening of great defensive sacrifice.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Ambrì wins 2-1 on Friborgo's ice - Müller and Schnarr score the decisive goals - Pestoni returns in place of the suspended Borradori - At 12', Miles Müller puts the blue-and-whites ahead
## Key facts - Result → 2-1 for Ambrì - Arena → BCF Arena - Return → Inti Pestoni - Absence → Tim Heed - Defense → six regular defensemen - Penalty kill → 66,6% before the game - Goaltending choice → Galley preferred to Waeber
After two consecutive home defeats, Ambrì were looking for crucial points in the den of the Swiss champions. At BCF Arena, the response came with a 2-1 victory, built on solidity, sacrifice and efficiency—in other words, the elements Tapola wanted to rediscover. The blue-and-whites thus conquered Friborgo's rink with full merit.
### A response after the home defeats
The lineup also presented some difficulties. Inti Pestoni returned to the lineup in place of the suspended Borradori, alongside Joly and Kodytek. In addition, Tapola had to deal with Tim Heed's absence, taking the ice with just six regular defensemen.
Despite the depleted defense, Ambrì started strongly, immediately putting the Swiss champions under pressure. Pestoni also looked dangerous, but was unable to beat Galley, preferred to Waeber. A penalty to Grassi in the offensive zone temporarily halted the Leventine side's momentum.
Friborgo's subsequent power play was neutralized by the blue-and-white penalty kill, though not without a few scares. Before the game, that special-teams situation was the worst in the League, with just 66,6% success.
At 12', Ambrì took the lead. Streule's mistake paved the way for Miles Müller, who made no mistake. Shortly afterward, Schmid hit a glaring post, but the visitors continued to create the best chances. The first period ended with Ambrì ahead and having rediscovered themselves after the last two outings. Müller and Schnarr's goals then decided an evening that ended with the blue-and-whites' 2-1 victory. ## The tactical key to victory
### Compactness, transitions and management of key moments
Ambrì's 2-1 win can be understood through a game plan that remained recognizable over the three periods. The team started strongly, maintained a compact and aggressive approach in the middle period and preserved the same identity at the start of the third period. The willingness to break forward accompanied the defensive phase without turning it into a passive approach.
The first element concerns precisely the ability to stick to Tapola's plan when Friborgo increased the pressure. The Swiss champions grew stronger in the middle period, but Wüthrich was ready on shots from Sörensen and Bertschy. At the same time, the blue-and-whites did not give up on the counterattack: Järventie found himself all alone in front of Galley with the puck for the second goal on his stick, but was unable to convert.
The second element is the management of the penalty kill. Grassi's penalty in the offensive zone had given Friborgo the opportunity to exploit the numerical advantage. The blue-and-white unit nevertheless neutralized the power play, despite a few moments of concern. The 66,6% figure makes this passage even more significant in the story of the game, because the special-teams situation entered the match as the worst in the League.
The third element is the resistance in the third period. Friborgo increased the pace, driven above all by Sörensen's line, but Ambrì responded with short shifts, great intensity and maximum focus. When the defense and Wüthrich were not enough, the post intervened once again: Nemeth's shot, shortly before the halfway point of the period, made the home cage tremble. The performance therefore stemmed from the balance between chances created, pressure absorbed and the ability to remain faithful to the game plan.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to read Ambrì's performance
### Four checks in the match report
To follow the game without focusing solely on the result, it is useful to start with the choices that defined the evening. The match report offers a precise sequence, useful for linking lineups, incidents and the team's response.
- Lineup and absences. The first step is to consider Inti Pestoni's return, brought in for the suspended Borradori, alongside Joly and Kodytek. In the same context, one must place Tim Heed's absence and the presence of just six regular defensemen.
- Start and special teams. The second step is to observe Ambrì's aggressive start, Pestoni's threat and Grassi's penalty in the offensive zone. The penalty kill should be read alongside the 66,6% recorded before the game and the ability to neutralize Fribourg's power play.
- Offensive incidents. The third step concerns efficiency. Streule's error paved the way for Miles Müller at 12', while Schmid's shot off the post and Järventie's chance in front of Galley show the other opportunities created by the blue-and-whites.
- Final pressure. The final check concerns the response to the pace imposed by Fribourg. Sörensen's line pushed forward, but Ambrì maintained short shifts, intensity and focus. Wüthrich dealt with the opponents' shots, and the post also denied Nemeth.
This framework makes it possible to read the performance through its essential stages, without separating Pestoni's return from the collective performance and without overlooking the importance of the chances that went unconverted. Follow Ambrì's next sports reports on Frontaliere Ticino.

item.title: Luino, bottle caps with nails in the parking lot behind Tigros
item.description: Paolo Nicastri reports the presence of caps with nails pointing upwards in the area used by cars, motorcycles and driving schools for driving exams and tests.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Corks with nails found in the parking lot behind Tigros - The points were facing upward - The area is used by cars, motorcycles and driving schools - The report was made by Paolo Nicastri
## Key facts - Location → parking lot behind Tigros in Luino - Objects → cork stoppers with nails pointing upward - Report → Paolo Nicastri - Role → former mayoral candidate in Luino - Elections → May 2026 - Use of the area → cars, motorcyclists and driving schools - Driving-school activities → practice sessions and exams for a motorcycle license
Some cork stoppers with nails inserted and the points facing upward were reportedly found in the parking lot behind Tigros in Luino. Paolo Nicastri, a young man from Luino and former candidate for mayor of Luino in the May 2026 municipal elections, made the discovery public through social media.
The site is frequented by cars and motorcyclists and is also used by driving schools for practice sessions and exams for a motorcycle license. The presence of the corks therefore concerns an area where different users move around and where practical training activities also take place.
In the published video, Nicastri shows some corks into which nails appear to have been inserted. The points are oriented upward. The young man from Luino highlights the risk that a motorcyclist might ride over them, puncture a tire and fall. His question in the video draws attention to the possible immediate consequences of those objects being present on the ground.
The focus of the report is the physical danger posed by the nails and the particular use of the parking lot. Nicastri links the discovery to the safety of those who use the area, with specific attention to students taking part in practice sessions and exams for a motorcycle license.
The report published on social media therefore starts from this concrete element: the presence of sharp objects, with the points facing upward, in a Luino parking lot frequented by cars, motorcycles and driving schools. ## A parking lot also used for motorcycle tests
The role of driving schools is the point Nicastri emphasizes most in the video. He does not merely recall that the parking lot is frequented by motorcyclists: he stresses that practice sessions and motorcycle license tests take place in the same space. The presence of the nails is therefore described in relation to those who might cross the area during a training or examination activity.
> It is precisely in this parking lot that driving schools conduct practice sessions and motorcycle license exams
In his reasoning, the risk concerns not only the possible fall of a young person on a motorcycle. Nicastri also raises the possibility that a driving-school vehicle could puncture one or more tires by driving over the nails. In that case, he observes, the danger to people would be accompanied by financial damage. The report is thus linked both to physical safety and to the material consequences for those who use the parking lot.
The video also refers to some complaints that, according to Nicastri, have concerned the area recently. The reference is not turned into an accusation against anyone. Instead, the young man from Luino asks that any disputes over the use of the area be handled without adopting behavior capable of endangering other people.
The message also addresses the issue of motorcycle enthusiasts. Nicastri wonders whether it is possible to identify a dedicated and safe space for them, alongside the discussion of the risks present in a parking lot used for traffic and driving-school activities.
The reaction described by the source therefore remains a position conveyed through social media: safety for those taking the tests, attention to possible tire damage, and a request not to let complaints about the area degenerate into dangerous acts. ## The clarification about who left the caps
Paolo Nicastri accompanies the report with a clear clarification regarding responsibility for the act. He says he does not know who left the objects in the parking lot and makes it clear that he does not want to accuse anyone without concrete evidence. In the video, he states that he has no proof. His report, therefore, does not identify anyone responsible and keeps the discovery of the caps separate from any possible attribution of the act.
This passage also defines the scope of the matter described by the source. The issue reported at present is the presence of cork stoppers with nails pointing upward and the danger they may pose to cars, motorcycles and driving schools. Nicastri does not identify who allegedly left them, focusing his report on the objects found and their position in the parking lot.
The video’s conclusion returns specifically to safety. For the former mayoral candidate, the combination of nails pointing upward and a parking lot frequented by vehicles and motorcyclists constitutes an enormous danger. In his words, the same assessment applies to an area where driving schools take students for practice sessions and motorcycle license exams.
The continuation documented by the source contains neither an indication of who did it nor any further reconstruction of the act. The report therefore remains focused on the alarm raised through social media and on the need, emphasized by Nicastri, not to put the health or lives of those passing through the parking lot at risk.
The position expressed is twofold: on the one hand, it reports the cork stoppers with their points facing upward as a concrete fact; on the other, it avoids turning the report into an accusation without evidence. The central fact remains the one stated in the video: those objects, in that location, can create a very serious risk for anyone using the parking lot.

item.title: Serious accident on the A2 in Coldrerio
item.description: Southbound rear-end collision: a 68-year-old woman was slightly injured, while the 73-year-old passenger is in serious condition.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Accident on Friday shortly before 15.30 on the A2 in Coldrerio - A car rear-ended a stationary articulated lorry in the emergency bay - The 73-year-old passenger was taken to hospital by helicopter - The A2 was closed and then reduced to one lane
## Key facts - Location → A2, southbound, Coldrerio area - Time → Friday, shortly before 15.30 - Driver → 68-year-old Swiss woman, resident in the Canton of Zurich - Passenger → 73-year-old Swiss man, resident in the Canton of Zurich - Conditions → woman slightly injured; man in serious condition - Traffic → temporary closure, then traffic on one lane - Responders → SAM, REGA, firefighters and cantonal police
### The initial account of the accident
On Friday afternoon, shortly before 15.30, a serious accident occurred on the A2 motorway in the southbound direction, in the Coldrerio area. The cantonal police reported that a 68-year-old Swiss woman, resident in the Canton of Zurich, rear-ended an articulated lorry stopped beside the carriageway, in the emergency bay. The causes of the collision will have to be established by the investigation.
Also travelling in the car was a 73-year-old Swiss passenger, likewise resident in the Canton of Zurich. After initial treatment, both were taken to hospital. The woman was taken by ambulance with minor injuries. The man, however, was transported by helicopter in serious condition; his life is in danger.
To allow rescue operations and the landing of the REGA helicopter, the carriageway was temporarily closed. Subsequently, traffic was funnelled into a single lane. The measure had a very significant impact on traffic.
The involvement of two people required two separate transports, by ambulance for the driver and by helicopter for the passenger. The difference in the modes of transport corresponds to the conditions reported by the police: minor injuries for the woman, serious condition for the man.
The rescue operation involved SAM rescuers, a REGA helicopter, firefighters from the Mendrisiotto rescue centre and the cantonal police. The investigation will have to establish the causes of the rear-end collision. ## Traffic difficulties in the Mendrisiotto
The temporary closure of the motorway and the subsequent reduction to a single lane had very significant consequences for traffic. At 5 p.m., the police advised against setting off southbound. The warning was issued while rescue operations had already affected mobility in the area.
### The roads affected
According to Viasuisse, in the late afternoon traffic was completely congested on all roads between Mendrisio and Genestrerio. The situation did not affect only the motorway route: the report also included the cantonal road between Mendrisio and Chiasso, the San Martino fork toward Melide and, in Lugano, the main roads in the city center.
| Area | Reported situation | |---|---| | Roads between Mendrisio and Genestrerio | Traffic completely congested | | Cantonal road between Mendrisio and Chiasso | Traffic completely congested | | San Martino fork toward Melide | Traffic completely congested | | Main roads in central Lugano | Traffic completely congested |
Viasuisse’s reports therefore covered a series of different connections: the stretch between the two centers of the Mendrisiotto, the cantonal road toward Chiasso, the road at the San Martino fork in the direction of Melide and the central streets of Lugano. All these points were completely congested in the late afternoon.
The picture provided by Viasuisse shows that the repercussions were not concentrated solely at the site of the accident. The closure and the switch to one lane affected traffic in several areas, while the police advice at 5 p.m. urged people to avoid traveling south.
The situation then improved after 8 p.m. This is the latest time-based update reported by the source on traffic conditions, following the congestion reported in the late afternoon. ## The investigation remains open
### The aftermath of the operation
The aftermath of the accident remains linked to the investigation into how it happened. The cantonal police indicated that it will have to establish the reasons why the motorist rear-ended the articulated lorry stopped in the emergency lay-by. The essential details of the reconstruction thus remain established: the collision occurred on the A2, heading south, in the territory of Coldrerio, with a heavy vehicle stopped at the side of the carriageway. The investigation will have to clarify the sequence of events that led to the collision.
The operational follow-up is already defined by the sequence of the rescue efforts. After receiving initial treatment, the two people were taken to hospital: the woman by ambulance and the man by helicopter. To allow the rescue operation and the landing of the REGA helicopter, the carriageway was temporarily closed; later, traffic was channelled into a single lane. SAM rescuers, the REGA helicopter, firefighters from the Mendrisiotto rescue centre and the cantonal police attended the scene.
The medical situation reported for the passenger also remains: the 73-year-old man was transported by helicopter in serious condition and his life is in danger. The 68-year-old woman, on the other hand, was taken to hospital by ambulance with minor injuries. The police statement therefore distinguishes between two different outcomes and leaves the follow-up of the investigation into how the accident happened open.
